COACTUPC.CBL

This program accepts and processes updates to credit card account and customer information entered by bank staff through an online screen.

COACTUPC is an interactive CICS online program that allows bank operations staff to modify existing credit card account details and associated customer profile data. The program presents a data entry screen pre-populated with current account information, validates all user-entered changes against a comprehensive set of business rules, and if valid, persists the updates to the account and customer records. It handles dual-entity updates — both the financial account attributes (credit limits, balances, status, dates) and the customer demographic attributes (name, address, SSN, date of birth, FICO score) — in a single transaction.

Business Rules
  • Account status must be explicitly Y (active) or N (inactive) — no other values permitted
  • Credit limit, cash credit limit, current balance, cycle credits, and cycle debits must be valid signed numeric amounts
  • Customer date of birth must be a valid calendar date with year, month, and day each independently validated
  • Card expiry date and reissue date must be valid calendar dates with all three components (year, month, day) validated
  • Account open date must be a valid calendar date
  • US Social Security Number is validated in three segments: Part 1 (3 digits) cannot be 000, 666, or 900-999; Part 2 (2 digits) and Part 3 (4 digits) must be numeric and non-zero
  • US phone number must conform to standard format (area code + exchange + number) with each segment independently validated as numeric
  • Customer name fields (first, middle, last) must contain alphabetic characters only
  • Address fields (line 1, line 2, city, state, zip code, country) must contain alphanumeric characters and are individually validated
  • The program detects whether any data has actually changed before writing to the database — a no-change submission is identified and handled separately
  • All mandatory fields must be populated — blank mandatory fields are flagged as a distinct error condition separate from invalid-format errors
  • The update covers two linked entities simultaneously: the financial account record and the customer demographic record, both must pass validation before any write occurs

9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST-EXIT

This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the customer data retrieval routine, marking the boundary where control returns to the calling process after customer demographic information has been looked up by customer number.

Lines 3797–3800

9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA

This paragraph captures a snapshot of the current account and customer data retrieved from the database, storing it as the 'before image' baseline. This baseline is used later to detect whether the bank operator has actually changed any values, preventing unnecessary database writes and enabling change-detection logic.

Lines 3801–3884

9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA-EXIT

This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the routine that captures and stores retrieved account and customer data into the working area. It is a structural placeholder that marks the end of the data-fetching process, allowing the program to return control cleanly to the calling logic.

Lines 3885–3887

9600-WRITE-PROCESSING

This paragraph performs the actual database write operation for a validated credit card account update, locking both the financial account and customer demographic records, checking for concurrent modifications, assembling the updated data, and persisting both records to the database — rolling back if either write fails.

Lines 3888–4104

9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT

This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account update write processing routine. It marks the end of the write operation block, allowing control to return cleanly to the calling logic after all database update steps have been completed.

Lines 4105–4108

9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC

This paragraph determines whether the bank operator has actually modified any account or customer data before allowing a database write to proceed. It compares every editable field on the update screen against the original values retrieved from the database, and if any difference is detected, flags the transaction as containing real changes and routes processing accordingly.

Lines 4109–4192

9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC-EXIT

This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the change-detection routine that determines whether the operator has actually modified any account or customer data. It also incorporates shared logic for capturing which function key the operator pressed to trigger the update action.

Lines 4193–4202

ABEND-ROUTINE

This paragraph handles unrecoverable system failures during the account update process. It ensures that when a fatal error occurs, a meaningful diagnostic message is recorded, the error is surfaced to operations staff, and the transaction is formally terminated with a recognisable failure code so that support teams can identify and investigate the incident.

Lines 4203–4225

ABEND-ROUTINE-EXIT

853 LINKAGE SECTION.
854 01 DFHCOMMAREA.
855 05 FILLER PIC X(1)
856 OCCURS 1 TO 32767 TIMES DEPENDING ON EIBCALEN.
857
858 PROCEDURE DIVISION.
859 0000-MAIN. Entry point of the main controlling paragraph for the account update transaction.
860
861
862 EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND Registers a safety net routine so that if the program crashes unexpectedly, a controlled error handler takes over instead of an unhandled system failure.
863 LABEL(ABEND-ROUTINE)
864 END-EXEC
865
866 INITIALIZE CC-WORK-AREA Clears all working storage areas used for card interaction, general processing, and inter-program communication to ensure no stale data from a previous transaction contaminates the current one.
867 WS-MISC-STORAGE
868 WS-COMMAREA
869 *****************************************************************
870 * Store our context
871 *****************************************************************
872 MOVE LIT-THISTRANID TO WS-TRANID Records the identity of the current transaction so it can be referenced in navigation and communication handoffs to other programs.
873 *****************************************************************
874 * Ensure error message is cleared *
875 *****************************************************************
876 SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF TO TRUE Clears any previously displayed confirmation or error message from the screen so the operator starts with a clean message area.
877 *****************************************************************
878 * Store passed data if any *
879 *****************************************************************
880 IF EIBCALEN IS EQUAL TO 0 Checks whether this is a brand-new entry into the program with no prior context — either the operator has just launched it for the first time, or they have arrived fresh from the main menu without re-entering.
881 OR (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM = LIT-MENUPGM
882 AND NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER)
883 INITIALIZE CARDDEMO-COMMAREA Resets all inter-program communication and program-specific session data to a clean state for a fresh start.
884 WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
885 SET CDEMO-PGM-ENTER TO TRUE Marks the session as a first-time entry, signalling that no account data has been loaded or processed yet.
886 SET ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED TO TRUE Flags that no account details have been retrieved from the database yet, prompting the program to ask the operator for search criteria.
887 ELSE
888 MOVE DFHCOMMAREA (1:LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) TO Restores the shared communication context passed from the previously active program, so the current program knows where it came from and what account was being worked on.
889 CARDDEMO-COMMAREA
890 MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1: Restores the program-specific session state (such as which step of the update workflow the operator was on) from the data passed between program calls.
891 LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA ) TO
892 WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
893 END-IF
894 *****************************************************************
895 * Remap PFkeys as needed.
896 * Store the Mapped PF Key
897 *****************************************************************
898 PERFORM YYYY-STORE-PFKEY Translates the raw keyboard input (the key the operator pressed) into a standardised function key code that the program can evaluate consistently.
899 THRU YYYY-STORE-PFKEY-EXIT
900 *****************************************************************
901 * Check the AID to see if its valid at this point *
902 * F3 - Exit
903 * Enter show screen again
904 *****************************************************************
905 SET PFK-INVALID TO TRUE Defaults the operator's key press to 'invalid' before checking whether it is actually an accepted action at this point in the workflow.
906 IF CCARD-AID-ENTER OR Checks whether the operator pressed Enter to submit data, F3 to exit, F5 to confirm a pending update, or F12 to go back — all of which are legitimate actions depending on the current screen state.
907 CCARD-AID-PFK03 OR
908 (CCARD-AID-PFK05 AND ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED)
909 OR
910 (CCARD-AID-PFK12 AND NOT ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED)
911 SET PFK-VALID TO TRUE Marks the key press as valid because it matched one of the accepted actions for the current workflow state.
912 END-IF
913
914 IF PFK-INVALID If the operator pressed a key that is not valid in the current context (e.g. an unsupported function key), treats the action as a plain Enter submission to prevent unintended navigation.
915 SET CCARD-AID-ENTER TO TRUE
916 END-IF
917
918 *****************************************************************
919 * Decide what to do based on inputs received
920 *****************************************************************
921 EVALUATE TRUE Begins the decision logic that routes the transaction to the correct processing path based on the operator's action and the current state of the update workflow.
922 ******************************************************************
923 * USER PRESSES PF03 TO EXIT
924 * OR USER IS DONE WITH UPDATE
925 * XCTL TO CALLING PROGRAM OR MAIN MENU
926 ******************************************************************
927 WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK03 Handles the case where the operator has pressed F3 to exit the account update screen and return to the calling program or main menu.
928 SET CCARD-AID-PFK03 TO TRUE
929
930 IF CDEMO-FROM-TRANID EQUAL LOW-VALUES Checks whether there is a specific transaction to return to; if not, defaults the destination to the main menu transaction.
931 OR CDEMO-FROM-TRANID EQUAL SPACES
932 MOVE LIT-MENUTRANID TO CDEMO-TO-TRANID Sets the navigation destination to the main menu transaction when no originating transaction was recorded.
933 ELSE
934 MOVE CDEMO-FROM-TRANID TO CDEMO-TO-TRANID Sets the navigation destination back to whichever transaction originally launched this update screen.
935 END-IF
936
937 IF CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM EQUAL LOW-VALUES Checks whether there is a specific program to return control to; if not, defaults the destination to the main menu program.
938 OR CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM EQUAL SPACES
939 MOVE LIT-MENUPGM TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM Sets the destination program to the main menu when no originating program was recorded in the session context.
940 ELSE
941 MOVE CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM Sets the destination program back to whichever program originally called this update screen.
942 END-IF
943
944 MOVE LIT-THISTRANID TO CDEMO-FROM-TRANID Records this update program as the origin of the handoff, so the receiving program knows where control came from.
945 MOVE LIT-THISPGM TO CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM Records the name of this update program in the communication area for the receiving program's reference.
946
947 SET CDEMO-USRTYP-USER TO TRUE Sets the user role context to standard operator (non-administrator) for the receiving program.
948 SET CDEMO-PGM-ENTER TO TRUE Marks the session state as a fresh entry so the receiving program initialises cleanly.
949 MOVE LIT-THISMAPSET TO CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET Records the current screen map set name in the communication area so the receiving program knows which screen was last active.
950 MOVE LIT-THISMAP TO CDEMO-LAST-MAP Records the current screen map name in the communication area for context handoff.

952 EXEC CICS Commits all database changes made during this transaction to ensure data integrity before transferring control away from this program.
953 SYNCPOINT
954 END-EXEC

956 EXEC CICS XCTL Transfers control to the destination program (main menu or calling program), passing the session context, effectively ending this program's execution.
957 PROGRAM (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM)
958 COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)
959 END-EXEC
960 ******************************************************************
961 * FRESH ENTRY INTO PROGRAM
962 * ASK THE USER FOR THE KEYS TO FETCH CARD TO BE UPDATED
963 ******************************************************************
964 WHEN ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED Handles the case where the operator has just arrived at the screen for the first time and no account data has been loaded yet — the program needs to display a blank entry screen to collect search criteria.
965 AND CDEMO-PGM-ENTER
966 WHEN CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM EQUAL LIT-MENUPGM Also handles the case where the operator has navigated here directly from the main menu without having previously entered this screen.
967 AND NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER
968 INITIALIZE WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA Resets the program-specific session data to ensure the operator starts with a completely fresh update form.
969 PERFORM 3000-SEND-MAP THRU Displays the account update screen to the operator, initially blank or with prompts, so they can enter the account number they wish to update.
970 3000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
971 SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER TO TRUE Marks the session as a re-entry so that on the next interaction the program knows the operator has already seen the screen once.
972 SET ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED TO TRUE Confirms that account details are still not loaded, keeping the program in the 'awaiting search criteria' state.
973 GO TO COMMON-RETURN Exits the main paragraph and returns control to CICS to wait for the operator's next input.
974 ******************************************************************
975 * ACCT DATA CHANGES REVIEWED, OKAYED AND DONE SUCESSFULLY
976 * RESET THE SEARCH KEYS
977 * ASK THE USER FOR FRESH SEARCH CRITERIA
978 ******************************************************************
979 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE Handles the case where a previous update attempt either completed successfully or failed — in both cases the program resets so the operator can start a new account update.
980 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-FAILED Also handles the failed update scenario in the same way as a completed update — reset and prompt for new search criteria.
981 INITIALIZE WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA Clears all session-specific data, general working storage, and the previously entered account identifier so the operator begins fresh.
982 WS-MISC-STORAGE
983 CDEMO-ACCT-ID
984 SET CDEMO-PGM-ENTER TO TRUE Marks the session as a fresh entry so the screen is presented in its initial state.
985 PERFORM 3000-SEND-MAP THRU Displays the account update screen again, cleared and ready for the operator to enter a new account number.
986 3000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
987 SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER TO TRUE Marks the session as a re-entry for the next interaction cycle.
988 SET ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED TO TRUE Resets the account-fetched indicator so the program knows it must retrieve account data again on the next submission.
989 GO TO COMMON-RETURN Exits the main paragraph and returns control to CICS to await the operator's next input.
990 ******************************************************************
991 * ACCT DATA HAS BEEN PRESENTED TO USER
992 * CHECK THE USER INPUTS
993 * DECIDE WHAT TO DO
994 * PRESENT NEXT STEPS TO USER
995 ******************************************************************
996 WHEN OTHER Handles all other situations — typically when account data is already displayed on screen and the operator has submitted changes for processing.
997 PERFORM 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS Validates all data the operator has entered on the update screen against the full set of business rules for account and customer fields.
998 THRU 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS-EXIT
999 PERFORM 2000-DECIDE-ACTION Evaluates the validation results and determines the next action — whether to save the changes, prompt for confirmation, or display error messages.
1000 THRU 2000-DECIDE-ACTION-EXIT
1001 PERFORM 3000-SEND-MAP Refreshes the screen with updated data, validation error highlights, confirmation prompts, or success messages depending on the outcome of processing.
1002 THRU 3000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
1003 GO TO COMMON-RETURN Exits the main paragraph and returns control to CICS to await the operator's next input.
1004 END-EVALUATE Closes the decision logic block that routed the transaction to the appropriate processing path.

1007 COMMON-RETURN. Entry point for the standard screen exit routine used at the end of every processing path.
1008 MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO CCARD-ERROR-MSG Places any pending confirmation or error message into the screen communication area so it will be visible to the operator on the next screen display.
1009
1010 MOVE CARDDEMO-COMMAREA TO WS-COMMAREA Loads the shared application-wide session context (current user, selected account, navigation state) into the outbound communication package to be passed forward.
1011 MOVE WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA TO Appends this program's own local session state — such as which screen fields were last active and what validation results were reached — into the outbound communication package immediately after the shared context.
1012 WS-COMMAREA(LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1: Positions the program-specific session data directly after the shared context block within the outbound communication package, ensuring both sections are preserved without overlap.
1013 LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA ) Specifies the exact length of the program-specific session data being appended, so the receiving program can correctly parse the two sections apart.
1014
1015 EXEC CICS RETURN Returns control to the CICS transaction manager, suspending the program while waiting for the operator's next screen interaction.
1016 TRANSID (LIT-THISTRANID) Instructs CICS to re-invoke this same account update transaction when the operator next presses a key, maintaining continuity of the update session.
1017 COMMAREA (WS-COMMAREA) Passes the complete session context — shared application state plus this program's local state — to the next invocation so no operator progress or validation results are lost.
1018 LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-COMMAREA) Declares the exact size of the session data being handed off, ensuring CICS allocates and transmits the full context without truncation.
1019 END-EXEC Closes the CICS return command block.

1021 0000-MAIN-EXIT. Defines the exit point label for the main account update processing routine — the logical end of the transaction's primary business flow.
1022 EXIT Signals the completion of all account and customer update processing, returning control to the CICS environment after validation and persistence steps are done.

1025 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS. Entry point for the full input processing routine that handles operator-submitted account and customer update data.
1026 PERFORM 1100-RECEIVE-MAP Reads all field values the bank operator has entered or modified on the account update screen into the program's working storage.
1027 THRU 1100-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT Marks the end of the screen data retrieval step.
1028 PERFORM 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS Runs the comprehensive business rule validation suite against every entered field — account status, financial amounts, dates, customer identity, and address data.
1029 THRU 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT Marks the end of the validation step; by this point all fields have been accepted or flagged with errors.
1030 MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO CCARD-ERROR-MSG Places any validation error message or confirmation notice into the communication area so it will be displayed to the operator on the next screen refresh.
1031 MOVE LIT-THISPGM TO CCARD-NEXT-PROG Signals that control should remain with this account update program after the screen is redisplayed, rather than returning to a menu or another program.
1032 MOVE LIT-THISMAPSET TO CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET Specifies that the same screen map set (the account update screen group) should be used when the screen is next displayed.
1033 MOVE LIT-THISMAP TO CCARD-NEXT-MAP Specifies that the same individual account update screen layout should be used for the next display, ensuring the operator sees their entered data with any error highlights.
1034 . Ends the paragraph and returns control to the calling routine.
1035 *
1036 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS-EXIT. Marks the end of the input processing and validation section — control returns to the main program flow after all user-entered changes have been assessed.
1037 EXIT Formally exits the input processing routine, signalling that all account and customer field validations have been completed and the program may proceed to the next stage.

1039 1100-RECEIVE-MAP. Entry point of the routine that collects all operator-entered changes from the account update screen.

1041 MAPSET(LIT-THISMAPSET) Identifies which screen layout definition to use when reading the operator's input.
1042 INTO(CACTUPAI) Directs the screen data into the program's working input buffer so individual fields can be examined.
1043 RESP(WS-RESP-CD) Captures whether the screen read succeeded or encountered a system-level problem.
1044 RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) Captures a secondary system response code for more detailed error diagnosis if the screen read fails.
1045 END-EXEC Ends the screen-read operation.

1426 1100-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT. Marks the end of the screen data reception routine — control returns to the section that invoked the data capture process.
1427 EXIT Formally exits the routine, signalling that all operator-entered updates have been collected and the program is ready to proceed to validation.
1428 .
1429 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS. Entry point for the screen input validation routine.
1430
1431 SET INPUT-OK TO TRUE Optimistically assumes all inputs are valid before beginning individual field checks.
1432
1433 IF ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED Checks whether account data has not yet been retrieved — meaning the operator has only entered search criteria, not yet confirmed which account to update.
1434 * VALIDATE THE SEARCH KEYS
1435 PERFORM 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT Validates the account number entered as the search key to ensure it identifies a real, retrievable account.
1436 THRU 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT
1437
1438 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO ACUP-OLD-ACCT-DATA Clears any previously held account data snapshot to ensure no stale data is carried forward before a fresh lookup.
1439
1440 * IF THE SEARCH CONDITIONS HAVE PROBLEMS FLAG THEM
1441 IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK Checks whether the operator submitted the screen without entering any account search criteria at all.
1442 SET NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED TO TRUE Flags the transaction as rejected because no account identifier was provided — the system cannot proceed without knowing which account to update.
1443 END-IF
1444
1445 * AT THIS STAGE. NO DETAILS FETCHED. NOTHING MORE TO EDIT.
1446 GO TO 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT Exits the validation routine early because no account data has been loaded yet — there is nothing further to validate at this stage.
1447 ELSE
1448 CONTINUE
1449 END-IF
1450 *
1451 * SEARCH KEYS ALREADY VALIDATED AND DATA FETCHED
1452 SET FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA TO TRUE Confirms that a matching account record has been successfully located and is available for editing.
1453 SET FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER TO TRUE Confirms that the account exists and was found in the account master file.
1454 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID TO TRUE Marks the account number search key as valid, clearing it from any prior error state.
1455
1456 SET FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER TO TRUE Confirms that the associated customer record was also found in the customer master file.
1457 SET FLG-CUSTFILTER-ISVALID TO TRUE Marks the customer number search key as valid, clearing it from any prior error state.
1458
1459 *
1460 PERFORM 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW Compares every field the operator entered against the original values on file to detect whether any actual changes were made.
1461 THRU 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW-EXIT
1462
1463 IF NO-CHANGES-FOUND Checks whether the operator made no changes, or has already confirmed and applied the changes, or is awaiting confirmation — in all these cases, no further field-level validation is needed.
1464 OR ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED
1465 OR ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE
1466 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS Clears all non-key validation flags to reset the screen state before exiting.
1467 GO TO 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT Exits the validation routine early because there is nothing new to validate or the update cycle is already complete.
1468 END-IF
1469
1470 SET ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK TO TRUE Marks the pending changes as not yet approved, requiring full field validation before any update can be committed.
1471
1472 MOVE 'Account Status' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the account active/inactive status field, for error reporting purposes.
1473 MOVE ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS TO WS-EDIT-YES-NO Passes the operator-entered account status value into the yes/no validation routine.
1474 PERFORM 1220-EDIT-YESNO Validates that the account status is explicitly set to active or inactive — no other value is acceptable.
1475 THRU 1220-EDIT-YESNO-EXIT
1476 MOVE WS-EDIT-YES-NO TO WS-EDIT-ACCT-STATUS Records the outcome of the account status validation for later use in determining whether the overall update can proceed.
1477
1478 MOVE 'Open Date' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the account opening date, for error reporting purposes.
1479 MOVE ACUP-NEW-OPEN-DATE TO WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD Passes the operator-entered account opening date into the date validation routine.
1480 PERFORM EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD Validates that the account opening date is a legitimate calendar date with valid year, month, and day components.
1481 THRU EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-EXIT
1482 MOVE WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS TO WS-EDIT-OPEN-DATE-FLGS Records the outcome of the account opening date validation for later use.
1483
1484 MOVE 'Credit Limit' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the total credit limit, for error reporting purposes.
1485 MOVE ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X TO WS-EDIT-SIGNED-NUMBER-9V2-X Passes the operator-entered credit limit amount into the signed numeric validation routine.
1486 PERFORM 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2 Validates that the credit limit is a properly formatted signed numeric monetary amount.
1487 THRU 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2-EXIT
1488 MOVE WS-FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-EDIT TO WS-EDIT-CREDIT-LIMIT Records the outcome of the credit limit validation for later use.
1489
1490 MOVE 'Expiry Date' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the card expiry date, for error reporting purposes.
1491 MOVE ACUP-NEW-EXPIRAION-DATE TO WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD Passes the operator-entered card expiry date into the date validation routine.
1492 PERFORM EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD Validates that the card expiry date is a legitimate calendar date with valid year, month, and day components.
1493 THRU EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-EXIT
1494 MOVE WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS TO WS-EXPIRY-DATE-FLGS Records the outcome of the card expiry date validation for later use.
1495
1496 MOVE 'Cash Credit Limit' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the cash advance credit limit, for error reporting purposes.
1497 MOVE ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-X Passes the operator-entered cash advance credit limit into the signed numeric validation routine.
1498 TO WS-EDIT-SIGNED-NUMBER-9V2-X
1499 PERFORM 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2 Validates that the cash advance credit limit is a properly formatted signed numeric monetary amount.
1500 THRU 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2-EXIT
1501 MOVE WS-FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-EDIT TO WS-EDIT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT Records the outcome of the cash advance credit limit validation for later use.
1502

1506 THRU EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-EXIT
1507 MOVE WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS TO WS-EDIT-REISSUE-DATE-FLGS Records the outcome of the card reissue date validation for later use.
1508
1509 MOVE 'Current Balance' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the current outstanding balance, for error reporting purposes.
1510 MOVE ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-X TO WS-EDIT-SIGNED-NUMBER-9V2-X Passes the operator-entered current balance into the signed numeric validation routine.
1511 PERFORM 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2 Validates that the current outstanding balance is a properly formatted signed numeric monetary amount.

1513 MOVE WS-FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-EDIT TO WS-EDIT-CURR-BAL Records the outcome of the current balance validation for later use.

1517 TO WS-EDIT-SIGNED-NUMBER-9V2-X
1518 PERFORM 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2 Validates that the current cycle credit amount is a properly formatted signed numeric monetary amount.
1519 THRU 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2-EXIT

1529 MOVE 'SSN' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the customer's Social Security Number, for error reporting purposes.
1530 PERFORM 1265-EDIT-US-SSN Validates the Social Security Number against US SSN rules: the first segment cannot be 000, 666, or in the 900-999 range, and all segments must be numeric and non-zero.
1531 THRU 1265-EDIT-US-SSN-EXIT

1538 MOVE WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS TO WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-FLGS Records the initial outcome of the date of birth format validation for later use.
1539 IF WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-ISVALID Checks whether the date of birth passed the basic calendar format check before applying deeper business-rule validation.
1540 PERFORM EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH Performs additional business-rule validation on the date of birth — for example, ensuring the customer is of a plausible age.
1541 THRU EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH-EXIT
1542 MOVE WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS TO WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-FLGS Updates the date of birth validation result with the outcome of the deeper business-rule check.
1543 END-IF

1545 MOVE 'FICO Score' TO WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME Labels the next validation as being for the customer's FICO credit score, for error reporting purposes.
1546 MOVE ACUP-NEW-CUST-FICO-SCORE-X Passes the operator-entered FICO score into the numeric validation routine.
1547 TO WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY
1548 MOVE 3 TO WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH Specifies that the FICO score is expected to be exactly 3 digits in length.
1549 PERFORM 1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD Validates that the FICO score field contains a required numeric value of the correct length.
1550 THRU 1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD-EXIT
1551 MOVE WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY-FLAGS Records the outcome of the FICO score format validation for later use.
1552 TO WS-EDIT-FICO-SCORE-FLGS
1553 IF FLG-FICO-SCORE-ISVALID Checks whether the FICO score passed the basic numeric format check before applying range validation.

1570 MOVE 25 TO WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH Specifies that the middle name field can be up to 25 characters long.

1783 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT. Entry point for the account number validation routine within the update transaction.
1784 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE Initialises the account number validation result to 'failed' as a safe default, so any exit without explicit approval leaves the transaction blocked.
1785
1786 * Not supplied
1787 IF CC-ACCT-ID EQUAL LOW-VALUES Checks whether the operator left the account number field completely empty (no data entered at all).
1788 OR CC-ACCT-ID EQUAL SPACES Also checks whether the account number field contains only blank spaces, treating it as equally missing.
1789 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall input submission as invalid, preventing the update from proceeding.
1790 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK TO TRUE Records the specific reason for rejection as a blank/missing account number, distinguishing it from a format error.
1791 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether a user-facing error message has already been set by a prior validation step, to avoid overwriting an earlier message.
1792 SET WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT TO TRUE Displays a prompt to the operator asking them to supply the required account number before resubmitting.
1793 END-IF
1794 MOVE ZEROES TO CDEMO-ACCT-ID Clears the account identifier held in the shared communication area and the screen's working copy, ensuring no stale or partial account reference is carried forward.
1795 ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID Continues clearing the account number from the screen update record as part of the same reset operation.
1796 GO TO 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT Exits the validation routine immediately, since there is nothing further to validate when no account number was provided.
1797 END-IF
1798
1799 * Not numeric
1800 * Not 11 characters
1801 MOVE CC-ACCT-ID TO ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID Copies the operator-entered account number into the screen's update record so it is available for further processing if validation passes.
1802 IF CC-ACCT-ID IS NOT NUMERIC Checks whether the entered account number contains any non-numeric characters, which would make it an invalid account identifier.
1803 OR CC-ACCT-ID-N EQUAL ZEROS Also checks whether the account number, though numeric in format, has a value of zero — which is not a valid account number in the system.
1804 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall submission as invalid because the account number fails the numeric or non-zero requirement.
1805 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether a user-facing error message has already been set, to avoid overwriting a previously recorded error.
1806 STRING Begins constructing a descriptive error message to inform the operator of the exact account number format requirement.
1807 'Account Number if supplied must be a 11 digit' First part of the error message text, stating that the account number must be an 11-digit value if provided.
1808 ' Non-Zero Number' Second part of the error message, clarifying that the 11-digit account number must also be non-zero.
1809 DELIMITED BY SIZE Specifies that the full field size is used when assembling the message, with no delimiter truncation.
1810 INTO WS-RETURN-MSG Writes the assembled error message into the operator message area so it will be displayed on the screen.
1811 END-IF
1812 MOVE ZEROES TO CDEMO-ACCT-ID Clears the account identifier from the shared communication area to prevent an invalid account number from being passed to downstream processing.
1813 GO TO 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT Exits the validation routine immediately after recording the format error, skipping the success path.
1814 ELSE
1815 MOVE CC-ACCT-ID TO CDEMO-ACCT-ID Copies the validated account number into the shared communication area so it is available to subsequent programs in the transaction flow.
1816 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID TO TRUE Records the account number validation result as successful, allowing the update process to continue to the next validation step.
1817 END-IF
1818 . Marks the end of the account number validation routine.

1821 EXIT Returns control to the part of the program that invoked the account validation routine, allowing the overall update process to continue to its next step.

2432 *Format xxx-xx-xxxx Documents the expected SSN format: three digits, hyphen, two digits, hyphen, four digits.
2433 *Part1 :should have 3 digits Documents that the first segment must contain exactly 3 numeric digits.
2434 *Part2 :should have 2 digits and it should be from 01 to 99 Documents that the second segment must contain exactly 2 numeric digits, ranging from 01 to 99.
2435 *Part3 should have 4 digits from 0001 to 9999. Documents that the third segment must contain exactly 4 numeric digits, ranging from 0001 to 9999.
2436 ******************************************************************
2437 * Edit SSN Part 1
2438 ******************************************************************

2441 MOVE 3 TO WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH Instructs the numeric validator to evaluate exactly 3 characters, matching the required length of the SSN area number segment.
2442 PERFORM 1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD Invokes the shared numeric validation routine to confirm the first SSN segment is present and contains only digits.

2446
2447 *Part1 :should not be 000, 666, or between 900 and 999

2449 MOVE ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1 TO WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1 Loads the validated first SSN segment value for comparison against the list of prohibited SSN area numbers.
2450 IF INVALID-SSN-PART1 Checks whether the first SSN segment contains a value that is federally prohibited: 000, 666, or any number from 900 to 999.

2515 IF FICO-RANGE-IS-VALID Checks whether the FICO credit score entered by the operator falls within the valid industry range of 300 to 850.
2516 CONTINUE If the score is within the valid range, no action is needed and processing continues normally.
2517 ELSE Begins the handling for the case where the FICO score is outside the acceptable range.
2518 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the entire update submission as invalid, preventing any changes from being saved to the database.
2519 SET FLG-FICO-SCORE-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the FICO credit score field specifically as failing validation, so the screen can highlight the offending field for the operator.
2520 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether an error message has already been set by a previous validation failure, to avoid overwriting an earlier error.
2521 STRING Begins composing a descriptive error message to display to the bank operator on screen.
2522 FUNCTION TRIM(WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME) Includes the name of the field that failed validation in the error message so the operator knows which value to correct.
2523 ': should be between 300 and 850' Appends the specific rule that was violated — the FICO score must be between 300 and 850 — to the error message.
2524 DELIMITED BY SIZE Specifies that the full allocated size of each text segment is used when building the message string.
2525 INTO WS-RETURN-MSG Directs the composed error message to the area displayed to the operator on the update screen.
2526 END-STRING Closes the message construction block.
2527 END-IF Closes the condition that checks whether a message slot is available.
2528 GO TO 1275-EDIT-FICO-SCORE-EXIT Exits the FICO score validation step immediately, skipping any remaining logic, since the field has already been found invalid.
2529 END-IF Closes the invalid-score handling block.
2530 . Marks the end of the FICO score validation paragraph.
2531 1275-EDIT-FICO-SCORE-EXIT. Marks the end of the FICO credit score validation section — this label signals where control returns to after all FICO score checks are complete.
2532 EXIT Formally exits the FICO score validation routine, returning control to the next step in the overall account update validation sequence.

2535 *A crude zip code edit based on data from USPS web site Developer comment indicating that the next section of code performs a basic zip code format check using reference data sourced from the US Postal Service website.
2536 1280-EDIT-US-STATE-ZIP-CD. Entry point for the state and ZIP code cross-validation routine.
2537 STRING ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD Begins assembling a lookup key using the customer's state code (e.g. 'CA', 'NY') entered on the update screen.
2538 ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-ZIP(1:2) Appends the first two digits of the customer's ZIP code to the state code, forming a combined key for geographic validation.
2539 DELIMITED BY SIZE Specifies that each component is taken at its full defined length with no delimiter trimming.
2540 INTO US-STATE-AND-FIRST-ZIP2 Stores the combined state-plus-ZIP-prefix key into the lookup buffer that will be checked against the valid state/ZIP reference table.
2541
2542 IF VALID-US-STATE-ZIP-CD2-COMBO Checks whether the combined state code and ZIP code prefix exists as a valid geographic combination in the reference table.
2543 CONTINUE If the state and ZIP code prefix are a valid geographic match, no action is needed and processing continues normally.
2544 ELSE
2545 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall screen input as containing an error, blocking the account update from proceeding.
2546 SET FLG-STATE-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the state code field as invalid so it can be highlighted on screen for the operator to correct.
2547 SET FLG-ZIPCODE-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the ZIP code field as invalid so it can also be highlighted on screen, since both fields contribute to the mismatch.
2548 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether a return message has already been set by a prior validation failure, to avoid overwriting an earlier error message.
2549 STRING Begins composing the error message to be displayed to the bank operator.
2550 'Invalid zip code for state' Sets the error message text informing the operator that the ZIP code entered does not correspond to the selected state.
2551 DELIMITED BY SIZE Specifies that the message text is taken at its full length.
2552 INTO WS-RETURN-MSG Writes the error message into the operator-facing message area that will appear on the update screen.
2553 END-STRING Closes the message composition block.
2554 END-IF Closes the conditional block that guards against overwriting an existing error message.
2555 GO TO 1280-EDIT-US-STATE-ZIP-CD-EXIT Exits the validation routine immediately, since the geographic mismatch is a terminal validation failure for this check.
2556 END-IF Closes the main validation conditional block.

2558 1280-EDIT-US-STATE-ZIP-CD-EXIT. Labels the exit point of the US state and ZIP code validation section, signalling that all state and ZIP code checks have been completed.
2559 EXIT Returns control to the part of the update process that invoked the state and ZIP code validation, allowing the overall input validation to continue.

2562 2000-DECIDE-ACTION. Entry point of the paragraph that orchestrates all decision-making for the account update workflow.
2563 EVALUATE TRUE Begins evaluating the current state of the update session to determine which business action to take next.
2564 ******************************************************************
2565 * NO DETAILS SHOWN.
2566 * SO GET THEM AND SETUP DETAIL EDIT SCREEN
2567 ******************************************************************
2568 WHEN ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED Handles the case where account and customer details have not yet been loaded onto the screen — the system needs to fetch and display the current record before any editing can occur.
2569 ******************************************************************
2570 * CHANGES MADE. BUT USER CANCELS
2571 ******************************************************************
2572 WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK12 Handles the case where the operator pressed the Cancel function key (F12) while changes were in progress, signalling an intent to abandon edits and revert to the original data.
2573 IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID Checks whether the account number entered on screen is valid and exists in the system before attempting to reload the original account data.
2574 SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF TO TRUE Clears any outstanding status or confirmation message from the screen so the operator sees a clean display when the original data is reloaded.
2575 PERFORM 9000-READ-ACCT Retrieves the current account and associated customer details from the master files so the screen can be repopulated with the original, unmodified information.
2576 THRU 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT Marks the end of the account retrieval routine.
2577 IF FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER Checks whether a matching customer record was successfully found in the customer master file for the given account.
2578 SET ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS TO TRUE Transitions the screen back to display mode, showing the original account and customer details, effectively discarding any unsaved changes the operator had made.
2579 END-IF
2580 END-IF
2581 ******************************************************************
2582 * DETAILS SHOWN
2583 * CHECK CHANGES AND ASK CONFIRMATION IF GOOD
2584 ******************************************************************
2585 WHEN ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS Handles the state where account details are currently displayed on screen and the operator has submitted changes for processing.
2586 IF INPUT-ERROR Checks whether the validation process found any errors in the data the operator entered, or whether no fields were actually changed from their original values.
2587 OR NO-CHANGES-DETECTED Also checks whether the submitted data is identical to what was already on file, meaning there is nothing new to save.
2588 CONTINUE If there are validation errors or no changes were detected, the workflow stays in its current state — the screen remains in edit mode with error indicators shown to the operator.
2589 ELSE
2590 SET ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED TO TRUE If all entered data passed validation and at least one field was changed, advances the workflow to the confirmation stage, prompting the operator to explicitly confirm before the update is written to the database.
2591 END-IF
2592 ******************************************************************
2593 * DETAILS SHOWN
2594 * BUT INPUT EDIT ERRORS FOUND
2595 ******************************************************************
2596 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK Handles the state where validation errors were found in the operator's input — the screen remains in an error state so the operator can correct the highlighted fields.
2597 CONTINUE No additional action is taken; the screen will be refreshed with error highlights already set by the validation routines, allowing the operator to correct their input.
2598 ******************************************************************
2599 * DETAILS EDITED , FOUND OK, CONFIRM SAVE REQUESTED
2600 * CONFIRMATION GIVEN.SO SAVE THE CHANGES
2601 ******************************************************************
2602 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED Handles the state where all changes have been validated and the system is awaiting the operator's explicit confirmation to save.
2603 AND CCARD-AID-PFK05 Checks that the operator pressed the designated Confirm/Save function key (F5) to authorise the update to proceed.
2604 PERFORM 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING Executes the save process, which writes the validated changes to both the financial account record and the customer demographic record in the database.
2605 THRU 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT Marks the end of the save processing routine.
2606 EVALUATE TRUE Evaluates the outcome of the save attempt to determine which result state to present to the operator.
2607 WHEN COULD-NOT-LOCK-ACCT-FOR-UPDATE Checks whether the save failed because the account record could not be exclusively locked for update, meaning another user or process was simultaneously accessing it.
2608 SET ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR TO TRUE Sets the screen to a lock-error state, informing the operator that the update could not be completed due to a record locking conflict.
2609 WHEN LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED Checks whether the record was successfully locked but the actual database write operation subsequently failed.
2610 SET ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED TO TRUE Sets the screen to a failure state, informing the operator that the record was reserved but the update itself did not complete successfully.
2611 WHEN DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE Checks whether the account or customer data was modified by another process between the time the operator loaded the screen and the time they submitted the save, creating a data conflict.
2612 SET ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS TO TRUE Reloads the screen with the most current data from the database so the operator can review the latest values and re-enter their intended changes against the updated baseline.
2613 WHEN OTHER Covers all other outcomes from the save attempt, which in normal processing means the update completed successfully.
2614 SET ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE TO TRUE Sets the screen to the success state, confirming to the operator that both the account and customer records have been updated and saved.
2615 END-EVALUATE
2616 ******************************************************************
2617 * DETAILS EDITED , FOUND OK, CONFIRM SAVE REQUESTED
2618 * CONFIRMATION NOT GIVEN. SO SHOW DETAILS AGAIN
2619 ******************************************************************
2620 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED Handles the case where the system is awaiting save confirmation but the operator did not press the Confirm key — they pressed some other key instead.
2621 CONTINUE No action is taken; the screen remains in the confirmation-pending state, continuing to prompt the operator to either confirm or cancel the pending update.
2622 ******************************************************************
2623 * SHOW CONFIRMATION. GO BACK TO SQUARE 1
2624 ******************************************************************
2625 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE Handles the state immediately after a successful save, resetting the workflow so the operator can begin a new update transaction.
2626 SET ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS TO TRUE Returns the screen to the initial detail-display mode, ready for the operator to look up and update another account.
2627 IF CDEMO-FROM-TRANID EQUAL LOW-VALUES Checks whether this update session was launched directly rather than being called from another menu or transaction in the application.
2628 OR CDEMO-FROM-TRANID EQUAL SPACES Continues the check for a standalone session launch with no originating transaction context.
2629 MOVE ZEROES TO CDEMO-ACCT-ID Clears the account number and card number from the shared communication area so the next session starts with a blank account lookup rather than re-displaying the just-updated account.
2630 CDEMO-CARD-NUM Continues clearing the card number as part of resetting the shared session context.
2631 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS Clears the account status indicator from the shared communication area, completing the reset of all account identifiers for the next operator interaction.
2632 END-IF
2633 WHEN OTHER Catches any unexpected combination of screen state and operator action that the program was not designed to handle.
2634 MOVE LIT-THISPGM TO ABEND-CULPRIT Records the identity of this program as the source of the unexpected condition for diagnostic purposes.
2635 MOVE '0001' TO ABEND-CODE Records a specific internal error code to identify this particular unexpected scenario in error logs.
2636 MOVE SPACES TO ABEND-REASON Clears the detailed reason field since no specific business reason applies to this unrecognised state.
2637 MOVE 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' Sets a descriptive error message indicating that the program encountered a data or state combination outside its defined business logic.
2638 TO ABEND-MSG Continues setting the error message text.
2639 PERFORM ABEND-ROUTINE Invokes the abnormal-termination routine to halt the transaction safely and log the error, preventing any partial or corrupt data from being written.
2640 THRU ABEND-ROUTINE-EXIT Marks the end of the abnormal-termination routine call.
2641 END-EVALUATE Closes the overall decision-evaluation block.
2642 . Marks the end of the paragraph, returning control to the calling section of the program.
2643 2000-DECIDE-ACTION-EXIT. Labels the exit boundary of the section responsible for deciding which business action to perform based on operator input.
2644 EXIT Formally closes the action-decision section, returning control to the next step in the overall transaction processing flow.

2649 3000-SEND-MAP. Entry point for the screen-sending process — begins the sequence of steps required to display the account update screen to the operator.

2651 THRU 3100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
2652 PERFORM 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS Populates the screen fields with the current account and customer data values — credit limits, balances, names, addresses, dates — so the operator sees the live record.
2653 THRU 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS-EXIT
2654 PERFORM 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG Composes and places the appropriate informational or status message on the screen, such as a validation error summary or a successful-update confirmation for the operator.
2655 THRU 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG-EXIT
2656 PERFORM 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS Applies field-level display attributes — such as highlighting mandatory fields, protecting read-only fields, or flagging fields that failed validation — to guide the operator visually.

2658 PERFORM 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS Sets the display attributes specifically for the informational message area, ensuring error or confirmation messages are visually distinct (e.g. highlighted or coloured) on the operator's screen.
2659 THRU 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS-EXIT
2660 PERFORM 3400-SEND-SCREEN Transmits the fully prepared screen to the operator's terminal, making all account data, messages, and field highlights visible for review or further data entry.
2661 THRU 3400-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT

2699 * INITIALIZE SEARCH CRITERIA
2700 IF CDEMO-PGM-ENTER Checks whether the program has just been entered fresh from the menu — if so, no screen population is needed at this stage.

2710 EVALUATE TRUE Begins a decision block to determine which version of the account and customer data to render on screen.
2711 WHEN ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED Handles the case where the account record has not yet been retrieved from the database — no data is available to display.

2723 THRU 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES-EXIT

2955 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG. Entry point for the routine that selects and sets the correct informational message for the operator.
2956 * SETUP INFORMATION MESSAGE Comment indicating this block prepares the on-screen guidance message shown to the operator.
2957 EVALUATE TRUE Begins evaluating the current processing state of the transaction to determine which message is appropriate.
2958 WHEN CDEMO-PGM-ENTER Checks whether the operator has just entered this screen fresh from the main menu.
2959 SET PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS TO TRUE If entering fresh, instructs the operator to provide the account and customer identifiers needed to look up the record.
2960 WHEN ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED Checks whether a previous attempt to retrieve the account and customer details was unsuccessful.
2961 SET PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS TO TRUE If the record was not found, again prompts the operator to re-enter the search identifiers to locate the correct account.
2962 WHEN ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS Checks whether the account details have been successfully retrieved and are now displayed on screen.
2963 SET PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES TO TRUE If details are showing, instructs the operator to review the data and enter any desired changes to the account or customer information.
2964 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK Checks whether the operator submitted changes that failed validation — i.e., one or more fields contained invalid data.
2965 SET PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES TO TRUE If changes were invalid, prompts the operator to correct the flagged fields and resubmit the update.
2966 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED Checks whether the operator's changes passed all validation rules but have not yet been confirmed for saving.
2967 SET PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION TO TRUE If changes are valid but unconfirmed, prompts the operator to review and confirm before the update is permanently written to the database.
2968 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE Checks whether the operator confirmed the changes and the update was successfully saved to both the account and customer records.
2969 SET CONFIRM-UPDATE-SUCCESS TO TRUE If the update completed successfully, displays a confirmation message informing the operator that the changes have been applied.
2970
2971 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR Checks whether the update was approved but failed because the account or customer record was locked by another process.
2972 SET INFORM-FAILURE TO TRUE If a record lock prevented the save, displays a failure notification so the operator knows the update did not complete.
2973 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED Checks whether the confirmed update attempt failed for any other reason beyond a record lock.
2974 SET INFORM-FAILURE TO TRUE If the update failed for any other reason, displays a failure notification to alert the operator that the changes were not saved.
2975 WHEN WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE Checks whether no specific processing state has been identified, acting as a catch-all fallback condition.
2976 SET PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS TO TRUE As a default fallback, prompts the operator to enter search identifiers, ensuring the screen always shows a meaningful instruction.
2977 END-EVALUATE Ends the state-evaluation block.

2982 . Marks the end of this paragraph.
2983 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG-EXIT. Marks the named exit point that concludes the informational message setup routine used during account update processing.

2986 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS. Entry point for the routine that configures all screen field attributes before the update screen is displayed to the operator.
2987
2988 * PROTECT ALL FIELDS Comment: first step is to lock every field on the screen so nothing is editable by default.
2989 PERFORM 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS Calls the sub-routine that sets every field on the account update screen to read-only/protected, establishing a safe baseline before selectively opening fields for editing.
2990 THRU 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS-EXIT
2991
2992 * UNPROTECT BASED ON CONTEXT
2993 EVALUATE TRUE Begins a decision block that determines which fields to unlock for editing based on the current state of the transaction.
2994 WHEN ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED Checks whether account details have not yet been retrieved — i.e., the operator has only entered an account number but no account data has been loaded yet.
2995 * Make Account Id editable
2996 MOVE DFHBMFSE TO ACCTSIDA OF CACTUPAI When no account data has been loaded, unlocks only the account number entry field so the operator can type or correct the account they wish to look up.
2997 WHEN ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS Checks whether the screen is displaying a successfully retrieved account record ready for editing, or whether previously submitted changes failed validation.
2998 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK
2999 PERFORM 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS When account details are displayed (either freshly loaded or returned with validation errors), calls the sub-routine that unlocks all editable account and customer fields so the operator can make or correct changes.
3000 THRU 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS-EXIT
3001 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED Checks whether the operator has reviewed their changes and confirmed intent to save, but the save has not yet been executed.
3002 WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE Checks whether the update has already been confirmed and successfully written to the database.
3003 CONTINUE When the transaction is in a confirmed or completed state, leaves all fields locked — no further editing is permitted at this stage.
3004 WHEN OTHER Handles any unexpected screen state not covered by the above conditions.
3005 MOVE DFHBMFSE TO ACCTSIDA OF CACTUPAI In any unrecognised screen state, unlocks only the account number field as a safe fallback, allowing the operator to re-enter an account to look up.
3006 END-EVALUATE Ends the field-protection decision block.
3007
3008 * POSITION CURSOR - ORDER BASED ON SCREEN LOCATION Comment: second step is to position the cursor on the most relevant field, working through fields in top-to-bottom screen order.
3009 EVALUATE TRUE Begins a decision block that determines where to place the cursor based on which field has a validation problem or which state the screen is in.
3010 WHEN FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA Checks whether account data was successfully found and loaded onto the screen.
3011 WHEN NO-CHANGES-DETECTED Checks whether the operator submitted the form but no data had actually been changed from the original values.
3012 MOVE -1 TO ACSTTUSL OF CACTUPAI When account data is displayed or no changes were detected, positions the cursor on the account status field (active/inactive) — the first meaningful editable field — prompting the operator to begin reviewing or entering data.
3013 WHEN FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK Checks whether the account number entered by the operator failed validation (invalid format or value).
3014 WHEN FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK Checks whether the account number field was left completely blank by the operator.
3015 MOVE -1 TO ACCTSIDL OF CACTUPAI When the account number is invalid or missing, positions the cursor on the account number entry field so the operator can correct it immediately.

3017 WHEN FLG-ACCT-STATUS-NOT-OK Checks whether the account active/inactive status field failed validation (value other than Y or N).
3018 WHEN FLG-ACCT-STATUS-BLANK Checks whether the account status field was left blank.

3170 * SETUP COLOR
3171 IF CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET EQUAL LIT-CCLISTMAPSET Checks whether the operator navigated to this screen from the account list screen, which affects how the account number field should be coloured.
3172 MOVE DFHDFCOL TO ACCTSIDC OF CACTUPAO When arriving from the account list, sets the account number field to the default (non-highlighted) colour, since the account was already selected from a list rather than typed manually.
3173 END-IF Ends the navigation-source colour check.
3174
3175 * Account Filter
3176 IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK Checks whether the account number entered by the operator failed validation.
3177 MOVE DFHRED TO ACCTSIDC OF CACTUPAO Highlights the account number field in red to alert the operator that the value entered is invalid.
3178 END-IF Ends the invalid account number colour check.
3179
3180 IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK Checks whether the account number field was left blank AND the operator has already attempted to submit the screen at least once.
3181 AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER
3182 MOVE '*' TO ACCTSIDO OF CACTUPAO Displays an asterisk in the account number field to visually mark it as a required field that was left empty.
3183 MOVE DFHRED TO ACCTSIDC OF CACTUPAO Highlights the blank account number field in red to draw the operator's attention to the missing mandatory value.
3184 END-IF Ends the blank account number colour and marker check.
3185
3186 IF ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED Checks whether account details were never loaded, the account number is blank, or the account number is invalid — any of which means there is no point applying field-level colours to the rest of the screen.
3187 OR FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK
3188 OR FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK
3189 GO TO 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT Exits the screen attribute setup routine early when no valid account has been identified, since there are no account or customer detail fields to colour-code.
3190 ELSE Otherwise, continues processing to apply colour attributes to all remaining account and customer detail fields.
3191 CONTINUE
3192 END-IF Ends the early-exit decision.

3437 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT. Labels the exit point of the screen attribute configuration routine, signalling that all field display properties for the account update screen have been fully applied.
3438 EXIT Formally ends the screen setup routine, returning control to whichever part of the program invoked the screen attribute configuration process.

3440
3441 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS. Entry point of the routine that sets all screen fields to protected (read-only) mode.
3442 MOVE DFHBMPRF TO ACCTSIDA OF CACTUPAI Applies the standard CICS 'protected' screen attribute to the account identifier field, preventing the operator from changing the account number.
3443 ACSTTUSA OF CACTUPAI Protects the account active/inactive status field — the operator cannot toggle the account between active and inactive.
3444 *Account Limits
3445 ACRDLIMA OF CACTUPAI Protects the total credit limit field — the maximum borrowing capacity cannot be altered.
3446 ACSHLIMA OF CACTUPAI Protects the cash advance credit limit field — the sub-limit for cash withdrawals cannot be changed.
3447 ACURBALA OF CACTUPAI Protects the current outstanding balance field — the live balance owed on the account is locked from manual entry.
3448 ACRCYCRA OF CACTUPAI Protects the current billing cycle credits field — credits posted this cycle cannot be manually overridden.
3449 ACRCYDBA OF CACTUPAI Protects the current billing cycle debits field — debits posted this cycle cannot be manually overridden.
3450 *Account dates
3451 OPNYEARA OF CACTUPAI Protects the year component of the account opening date — the year the account was established cannot be edited.

3453 OPNDAYA OF CACTUPAI Protects the day component of the account opening date — the exact day the account was opened cannot be edited.

3459 RISDAYA OF CACTUPAI Protects the day component of the card reissue/renewal date — the day the card was last renewed cannot be edited.

3484 ACSPH1AA OF CACTUPAI Protects the area code segment of the customer's primary phone number — cannot be edited.

3486 ACSPH1CA OF CACTUPAI Protects the subscriber number segment of the customer's primary phone number — cannot be edited.
3487 ACSPH2AA OF CACTUPAI Protects the area code segment of the customer's secondary phone number — cannot be edited.
3488 ACSPH2BA OF CACTUPAI Protects the exchange segment of the customer's secondary phone number — cannot be edited.

3491 ACSGOVTA OF CACTUPAI Protects the government/regulatory classification field associated with the customer — cannot be changed.

3566 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS. Entry point for the routine that controls how the screen's status indicators and action prompts are visually rendered for the operator.
3567 IF WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE Checks whether there is currently no informational message to display to the bank operator on the update screen.
3568 MOVE DFHBMDAR TO INFOMSGA OF CACTUPAI If no informational message is present, dims or hides the message display area on screen so it does not distract the operator with blank or irrelevant content.
3569 ELSE Begins the alternative branch — a message does exist and needs to be drawn to the operator's attention.
3570 MOVE DFHBMASB TO INFOMSGA OF CACTUPAI If an informational message is present, highlights or brightens the message area on screen so the operator clearly sees the status notification or guidance text.
3571 END-IF Closes the conditional block governing the message area display attribute.
3572
3573 IF ACUP-CHANGES-MADE Checks whether the operator has made changes to the account or customer data on screen that have not yet been fully processed.
3574 AND NOT ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE Confirms that those pending changes have not already been confirmed and successfully saved to the database — i.e., the update is still awaiting operator confirmation.
3575 MOVE DFHBMASB TO FKEY12A OF CACTUPAI Highlights the 'Confirm/Save' function key indicator on screen, signalling to the operator that pressing it is required to finalise and commit the pending changes.
3576 END-IF Closes the conditional block for pending-changes key highlighting.
3577
3578 IF PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION Checks whether the screen is currently in a state where the operator must explicitly confirm their intended changes before the update is written to the database.
3579 MOVE DFHBMASB TO FKEY05A OF CACTUPAI Highlights the 'Cancel/Back' function key indicator, making it visually prominent so the operator can choose to abandon the pending update if desired.
3580 MOVE DFHBMASB TO FKEY12A OF CACTUPAI Highlights the 'Confirm/Save' function key indicator simultaneously, presenting the operator with a clear binary choice: confirm or cancel the pending account update.
3581 END-IF Closes the conditional block for the confirmation-prompt key highlighting.

3589 3400-SEND-SCREEN. This paragraph renders the account update screen to the bank operator's terminal, displaying all current account and customer data (including any validation error highlights) so the operator can review, correct, or confirm the information before submitting changes.

3591 MOVE LIT-THISMAPSET TO CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET Identifies which screen set (the account update screen group) should be displayed to the operator.

3595 MAPSET(CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET) Specifies the screen group containing the account update layout to be sent.
3596 FROM(CACTUPAO) Supplies the fully populated screen data — including account details, customer information, and any error indicators — as the content to display.
3597 CURSOR Positions the terminal cursor at the first field requiring operator attention, guiding the operator to where input or correction is needed.
3598 ERASE Clears any previously displayed content from the terminal before rendering the updated screen, ensuring a clean display.
3599 FREEKB Unlocks the terminal keyboard after the screen is sent, allowing the operator to begin entering or correcting data immediately.
3600 RESP(WS-RESP-CD) Captures the outcome of the screen transmission so the program can detect and handle any display failure.

3608 9000-READ-ACCT. Entry point for the account data retrieval process.
3609
3610 INITIALIZE ACUP-OLD-DETAILS Clears any previously held 'before-image' account and customer details to ensure the screen is populated only with fresh data from the database.
3611
3612 SET WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE TO TRUE Resets the screen message area to blank, clearing any prior informational messages before the retrieval begins.
3613
3614 MOVE CC-ACCT-ID TO ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID Copies the account number entered by the operator into both the working record that will hold the original account details and the cross-reference lookup key used to find the associated card.
3615 WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID
3616
3617 PERFORM 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT Looks up the credit card cross-reference file using the account number to confirm the account has a valid card on file and to retrieve the linked customer identifier.
3618 THRU 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT-EXIT End of the card cross-reference lookup routine.
3619
3620 IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK Checks whether the card cross-reference lookup failed — meaning no valid card record was found for the entered account number.
3621 GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT If no card cross-reference record exists for this account, abandons the retrieval immediately and exits without populating the screen, preventing the operator from updating a non-existent account.
3622 END-IF
3623
3624 PERFORM 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT Retrieves the full financial account record — including credit limits, balances, status, and dates — from the account master file using the account number.
3625 THRU 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT-EXIT End of the account master data retrieval routine.
3626
3627 IF DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT Checks whether the account master file lookup returned no matching record for the given account number.
3628 GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT If the account does not exist in the account master file, abandons the retrieval and exits, preventing any update attempt on an account with no financial record.
3629 END-IF
3630
3631 MOVE CDEMO-CUST-ID TO WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID Transfers the customer identifier obtained from the card cross-reference lookup into the key used to retrieve the customer's demographic record.
3632
3633 PERFORM 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST Retrieves the full customer demographic record — including name, address, date of birth, SSN, and FICO score — from the customer master file using the customer identifier linked to this account.
3634 THRU 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST-EXIT End of the customer demographic data retrieval routine.
3635
3636 IF DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT Checks whether the customer master file lookup returned no matching record for the customer linked to this account.
3637 GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT If the customer demographic record cannot be found, abandons the retrieval and exits, ensuring the operator cannot submit an update when the customer profile is missing.
3638 END-IF

3643 THRU 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA-EXIT End of the data storage routine.

3647 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT. Marks the end of the account retrieval routine — any branching logic that finishes reading account data lands here before returning to the main process flow.
3648 EXIT Signals the clean conclusion of the account read operation, returning control to whichever part of the update process invoked the account retrieval step.
