3650 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT. Entry point for the card cross-reference lookup routine, triggered when the program needs to resolve an account number to its linked card and customer.
3651
3652 * Read the Card file. Access via alternate index ACCTID
3653 *
3654 EXEC CICS READ Initiates a database read operation to retrieve the card cross-reference record that links an account number to its associated card and customer.
3655 DATASET (LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH) Specifies that the lookup is performed against the card cross-reference file using the account number as the search key (alternate index path).
3656 RIDFLD (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) Provides the account number entered by the operator as the search key to locate the matching cross-reference record.
3657 KEYLENGTH (LENGTH OF WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) Specifies the exact length of the account number being used as the search key, ensuring precise record matching.
3658 INTO (CARD-XREF-RECORD) Designates the memory area where the retrieved card cross-reference record will be stored for further processing.
3659 LENGTH (LENGTH OF CARD-XREF-RECORD) Specifies the expected size of the cross-reference record to be retrieved from the file.
3660 RESP (WS-RESP-CD) Captures the primary outcome code from the file read, indicating whether the lookup succeeded or encountered a problem.
3661 RESP2 (WS-REAS-CD) Captures a secondary diagnostic code providing additional detail about the outcome of the file read operation.
3662 END-EXEC
3663
3664 EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD Evaluates the result of the cross-reference file lookup to determine the appropriate business response.
3665 WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) Handles the successful case where the account number was found in the cross-reference file.
3666 MOVE XREF-CUST-ID TO CDEMO-CUST-ID Records the customer identifier linked to this account into the shared transaction context, making it available for the customer record update.
3667 MOVE XREF-CARD-NUM TO CDEMO-CARD-NUM Records the credit card number linked to this account into the shared transaction context, making it available for subsequent card-level processing.
3668 WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) Handles the case where the account number does not exist in the card cross-reference file — no matching card or customer link was found.
3669 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall input as invalid, preventing any update from being written to the database due to the unresolvable account reference.
3670 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the account identifier as failing validation, signalling that the account-to-card linkage could not be established.
3671 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether an error message has already been prepared for the operator, to avoid overwriting an earlier, more relevant error.
3672 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP Captures the primary error code from the failed lookup to include in the diagnostic message shown to the operator.
3673 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2 Captures the secondary error detail code from the failed lookup to provide additional context in the operator message.
3674 STRING Begins constructing a descriptive error message to inform the operator that the account could not be found in the cross-reference file.
3675 'Account:' Adds the label 'Account:' to the error message to identify what type of record was not found.
3676 WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X Inserts the specific account number that was searched, so the operator can verify the value they entered.
3677 ' not found in' Adds explanatory text indicating the account was not located in the cross-reference file.
3678 ' Cross ref file. Resp:' Continues the message text, identifying the cross-reference file as the source of the lookup failure and introducing the system response code.
3679 ERROR-RESP Embeds the primary system response code in the error message to assist technical support in diagnosing the failure.
3680 ' Reas:' Adds a label for the secondary reason code in the error message.
3681 ERROR-RESP2 Embeds the secondary diagnostic reason code in the error message for additional troubleshooting detail.
3682 DELIMITED BY SIZE Specifies that each component of the error message is included in full without truncation.
3683 INTO WS-RETURN-MSG Directs the fully assembled error message to the operator-facing message area so it will be displayed on screen.
3684 END-STRING Closes the message construction block.
3685 END-IF
3686 WHEN OTHER Handles any unexpected or system-level error that occurred while attempting to read the cross-reference file.
3687 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall input as invalid due to an unexpected file access failure, blocking the update from proceeding.
3688 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the account identifier as failing validation because the cross-reference file could not be successfully accessed.
3689 MOVE 'READ' TO ERROR-OPNAME Records that the failure occurred during a file read operation, for inclusion in the system error message.
3690 MOVE LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH TO ERROR-FILE Records the name of the cross-reference file that could not be read, for inclusion in the system error message.
3691 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP Captures the primary system error code from the failed file access for diagnostic reporting.
3692 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2 Captures the secondary system error detail code from the failed file access for diagnostic reporting.
3693 MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG Populates the operator-facing message area with a standard file error message describing the unexpected access failure.
3694 * WS-LONG-MSG
3695 * PERFORM SEND-LONG-TEXT
3696 END-EVALUATE
3697 .
3698 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT-EXIT. Labels the exit point of the card-to-account cross-reference lookup routine, signalling that all lookup processing has concluded.
3699 EXIT Formally ends the card cross-reference lookup routine, returning control to whichever part of the update process invoked it.
3700 .
3701 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT. Entry point for the account master file lookup routine.
3702
3703 EXEC CICS READ Initiates a direct read of the account master file to retrieve the account's financial details.
3704 DATASET (LIT-ACCTFILENAME) Specifies the account master file as the data source for this lookup.
3705 RIDFLD (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) Uses the account number entered by the operator as the search key to locate the correct account record.
3706 KEYLENGTH (LENGTH OF WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) Specifies the exact length of the account number to ensure a precise match in the file index.
3707 INTO (ACCOUNT-RECORD) Directs the retrieved account data into the working account record area for subsequent validation and display.
3708 LENGTH (LENGTH OF ACCOUNT-RECORD) Specifies the expected size of the account record to be read from the file.
3709 RESP (WS-RESP-CD) Captures the outcome code of the file read operation to determine whether it succeeded or failed.
3710 RESP2 (WS-REAS-CD) Captures a secondary diagnostic code providing additional detail if the file read did not complete normally.
3711 END-EXEC Closes the file read instruction block.
3712
3713 EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD Evaluates the outcome of the account file lookup to determine the appropriate business response.
3714 WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) Handles the successful case where the account was found in the master file.
3715 SET FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER TO TRUE Records that the account was successfully located, allowing the update process to continue.
3716 WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) Handles the case where the account number entered by the operator does not exist in the master file.
3717 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall input as invalid, blocking the account update from proceeding.
3718 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the account number field specifically as failing validation, so the screen can highlight the problematic field.
3719 * SET DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT TO TRUE
3720 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether a return message has already been set, to avoid overwriting an earlier error message.
3721 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP Records the primary file system response code for inclusion in the operator error message.
3722 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2 Records the secondary diagnostic code for inclusion in the operator error message.
3723 STRING Begins constructing a descriptive error message to inform the operator of the lookup failure.
3724 'Account:' Adds a label identifying that the following value is the account number that was not found.
3725 WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X Inserts the specific account number entered by the operator into the error message.
3726 ' not found in' Adds explanatory text indicating the account could not be located.
3727 ' Acct Master file.Resp:' Identifies the account master file as the source where the account was expected to be found, and labels the response code.
3728 ERROR-RESP Inserts the primary file system response code into the error message for diagnostic purposes.
3729 ' Reas:' Labels and prepares to insert the secondary reason code into the error message.
3730 ERROR-RESP2 Inserts the secondary diagnostic reason code into the error message.
3731 DELIMITED BY SIZE Specifies that each text segment is used in full without truncation when building the message.
3732 INTO WS-RETURN-MSG Directs the fully assembled error message to the area used to display feedback to the operator on screen.
3733 END-STRING Closes the message construction block.
3734 END-IF Closes the condition that guards against overwriting an existing error message.
3735 *
3736 WHEN OTHER Handles any unexpected file system error other than a normal read or a simple not-found condition.
3737 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall input as invalid due to an unexpected system-level file error.
3738 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the account identifier as unresolvable due to the unexpected file error.
3739 MOVE 'READ' TO ERROR-OPNAME Records that the failed operation was a file read, for inclusion in the system error message.
3740 MOVE LIT-ACCTFILENAME TO ERROR-FILE Records the name of the account master file where the error occurred, for diagnostic reporting.
3741 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP Captures the primary system response code describing the nature of the unexpected file error.
3742 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2 Captures the secondary diagnostic code providing further detail on the unexpected file error.
3743 MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG Populates the operator-facing message with a standard file error notification for display on screen.
3744 * WS-LONG-MSG
3745 * PERFORM SEND-LONG-TEXT
3746 END-EVALUATE Closes the outcome evaluation block, completing all error-handling branches for the account lookup.
3747 .
3748 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT-EXIT. Defines the exit label for the account data retrieval routine, acting as the designated return point after account lookup processing is finished.
3749 EXIT Signals the end of the account retrieval routine, returning control to whichever part of the update process invoked the account lookup.

3752 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST. Entry point for the routine that fetches customer profile data from the customer master file.
3753 EXEC CICS READ Initiates a direct read of the customer master file to retrieve the customer's demographic record.
3754 DATASET (LIT-CUSTFILENAME) Specifies the customer master file as the target data source for this lookup.
3755 RIDFLD (WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X) Uses the customer ID linked to the card account being updated as the search key to locate the correct customer record.
3756 KEYLENGTH (LENGTH OF WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X) Specifies the exact length of the customer ID key to ensure a precise, unambiguous match in the file.
3757 INTO (CUSTOMER-RECORD) Directs the retrieved customer demographic data (name, address, SSN, date of birth, etc.) into the working storage area for further processing.
3758 LENGTH (LENGTH OF CUSTOMER-RECORD) Specifies the expected size of the customer record to be read from the file.
3759 RESP (WS-RESP-CD) Captures the primary outcome code from the file read operation to determine whether the retrieval succeeded or failed.
3760 RESP2 (WS-REAS-CD) Captures a secondary diagnostic code that provides additional detail if the file read did not complete successfully.
3761 END-EXEC Closes the file read operation block.
3762
3763 EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD Evaluates the outcome of the customer file read to determine the appropriate business response.
3764 WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) Handles the successful case where the customer record was found and read without errors.
3765 SET FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER TO TRUE Records that the customer was successfully located in the customer master file, allowing the update process to continue.
3766 WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) Handles the case where no customer record exists for the provided customer ID.
3767 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall transaction input as invalid, preventing any updates from being written to the database.
3768 SET FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the customer identifier as failing validation, indicating the customer could not be verified in the master file.
3769 * SET DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT TO TRUE
3770 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP Preserves the primary error code from the failed file read for diagnostic and error reporting purposes.
3771 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2 Preserves the secondary diagnostic code from the failed file read to support detailed error investigation.
3772 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether a return message has already been set, to avoid overwriting an earlier error message displayed to the operator.
3773 STRING Begins composing a descriptive error message to inform the bank operator of the specific lookup failure.
3774 'CustId:' Adds a label identifying the customer ID component of the error message.
3775 WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X Includes the actual customer ID value that could not be found, so the operator knows exactly which customer was searched.
3776 ' not found' Appends text confirming that the customer ID was not found in the file.
3777 ' in customer master.Resp: ' Adds context indicating the search was performed against the customer master file.
3778 ERROR-RESP Appends the primary error code to the message to assist technical support in diagnosing the failure.
3779 ' REAS:' Adds a label for the secondary diagnostic reason code in the error message.
3780 ERROR-RESP2 Appends the secondary diagnostic code to give a complete technical picture of why the lookup failed.
3781 DELIMITED BY SIZE Specifies that each text segment is included in full without truncation when building the error message.
3782 INTO WS-RETURN-MSG Directs the fully assembled error message to the field that will be displayed to the bank operator on screen.
3783 END-STRING Closes the error message construction block.
3784 END-IF Closes the conditional check that guards against overwriting an existing error message.
3785 WHEN OTHER Handles any unexpected or system-level error that occurred during the customer file read, beyond a simple 'not found' condition.
3786 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the transaction as invalid due to an unexpected system error, blocking any database updates.
3787 SET FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE Flags the customer lookup as failed due to the unexpected system error.
3788 MOVE 'READ' TO ERROR-OPNAME Records that the failure occurred during a file read operation, for inclusion in the system error report.
3789 MOVE LIT-CUSTFILENAME TO ERROR-FILE Records the name of the customer master file where the error occurred, to assist in technical diagnosis.
3790 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP Captures the primary system error code returned by the failed file operation for error reporting.
3791 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2 Captures the secondary diagnostic code from the system error for detailed technical investigation.
3792 MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG Populates the operator-facing message with a standard file error description to inform staff that a system-level problem prevented the customer lookup.
3793 * WS-LONG-MSG
3794 * PERFORM SEND-LONG-TEXT
3795 END-EVALUATE Closes the outcome evaluation block, completing all error handling branches for the customer file read.
3796 . Marks the end of this paragraph and returns control to the calling routine.
3797 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST-EXIT. Defines the exit label for the customer data retrieval routine, acting as the designated return point once customer lookup processing is complete.
3798 EXIT Signals the end of the customer data retrieval process, returning control to whichever part of the account update workflow invoked this lookup routine.
3799 . Closes the paragraph definition, formally concluding the customer retrieval exit routine.

3801 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA. This paragraph captures a snapshot of the current account and customer data retrieved from the database, storing it as the 'before image' baseline. This baseline is used later to detect whether the bank operator has actually changed any values, preventing unnecessary database writes and enabling change-detection logic.
3802
3803 * Store Context in Commarea
3804 *
3805 MOVE ACCT-ID TO CDEMO-ACCT-ID Records the credit card account identifier into the shared session context so downstream programs and screens can reference which account is being worked on.
3806 MOVE CUST-ID TO CDEMO-CUST-ID Records the customer identifier into the shared session context to maintain the link between the account and its owner throughout the transaction.
3807 MOVE CUST-FIRST-NAME TO CDEMO-CUST-FNAME Stores the customer's first name into the shared session context for display and reference across subsequent screen interactions.
3808 MOVE CUST-MIDDLE-NAME TO CDEMO-CUST-MNAME Stores the customer's middle name into the shared session context for display and reference across subsequent screen interactions.
3809 MOVE CUST-LAST-NAME TO CDEMO-CUST-LNAME Stores the customer's last name into the shared session context for display and reference across subsequent screen interactions.
3810 MOVE ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS TO CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS Records the account's current active or inactive status into the shared session context so it is available for comparison and display.
3811 MOVE XREF-CARD-NUM TO CDEMO-CARD-NUM Records the physical credit card number associated with this account into the shared session context for reference during the update session.
3812
3813 INITIALIZE ACUP-OLD-DETAILS Clears and resets the entire 'before image' data area to ensure no residual data from a previous transaction contaminates the baseline snapshot about to be captured.
3814 ******************************************************************
3815 * Account Master data
3816 ******************************************************************
3817 MOVE ACCT-ID TO ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID Saves the account identifier as the baseline reference value, establishing which account record this snapshot belongs to.
3818 * Active Status
3819 MOVE ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS TO ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS Saves the account's current active or inactive status as the baseline, so any operator change to this field can be detected by comparison.
3820 * Current Balance
3821 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N Saves the account's current outstanding balance as the baseline, enabling detection of any operator modification to this financial figure.
3822 * Credit Limit
3823 MOVE ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT TO ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N Saves the account's current total credit limit as the baseline, enabling detection of any operator modification to this lending threshold.
3824 * Cash Limit
3825 MOVE ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT TO ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N Saves the account's current cash advance credit limit as the baseline, enabling detection of any operator modification to this sub-limit.
3826 * Current Cycle Credit
3827 MOVE ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT TO ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N Saves the total credits posted to the account in the current billing cycle as the baseline for change detection.
3828 * Current Cycle Debit
3829 MOVE ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT TO ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N Saves the total debits posted to the account in the current billing cycle as the baseline for change detection.
3830 * Open date
3831 * MOVE ACCT-OPEN-DATE TO ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DATE
3832 MOVE ACCT-OPEN-DATE(1:4) TO ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR Saves the four-digit year component of the account opening date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3833 MOVE ACCT-OPEN-DATE(6:2) TO ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON Saves the two-digit month component of the account opening date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3834 MOVE ACCT-OPEN-DATE(9:2) TO ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY Saves the two-digit day component of the account opening date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3835 * Expiry date
3836 * MOVE ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE TO ACUP-OLD-EXPIRAION-DATE
3837 MOVE ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE(1:4) TO ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR Saves the four-digit year component of the card expiry date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3838 MOVE ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE(6:2) TO ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON Saves the two-digit month component of the card expiry date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3839 MOVE ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE(9:2) TO ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY Saves the two-digit day component of the card expiry date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3840
3841 * Reissue date
3842 * MOVE ACCT-REISSUE-DATE TO ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DATE
3843 MOVE ACCT-REISSUE-DATE(1:4) TO ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR Saves the four-digit year component of the card reissue or renewal date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3844 MOVE ACCT-REISSUE-DATE(6:2) TO ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON Saves the two-digit month component of the card reissue or renewal date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3845 MOVE ACCT-REISSUE-DATE(9:2) TO ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY Saves the two-digit day component of the card reissue or renewal date as part of the baseline snapshot.
3846 * Account Group
3847 MOVE ACCT-GROUP-ID TO ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID Saves the account group or portfolio classification code as the baseline, enabling detection of any operator change to this categorisation.
3848 ******************************************************************
3849 * Customer Master data
3850 ******************************************************************
3851 *Customer Id (actually not editable)
3852 MOVE CUST-ID TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID Saves the customer identifier as part of the customer demographic baseline; this field is display-only and cannot be edited by the operator.
3853 *Social Security Number
3854 MOVE CUST-SSN TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-SSN Saves the customer's Social Security Number as the baseline for change detection during the update session.
3855 *Date of birth
3856 * MOVE CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD
3857 MOVE CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD(1:4) TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YEAR Saves the four-digit year component of the customer's date of birth as part of the demographic baseline snapshot.
3858 MOVE CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD(6:2) TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-MON Saves the two-digit month component of the customer's date of birth as part of the demographic baseline snapshot.
3859 MOVE CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD(9:2) TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-DAY Saves the two-digit day component of the customer's date of birth as part of the demographic baseline snapshot.
3860 *FICO
3861 MOVE CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-FICO-SCORE Saves the customer's current FICO credit score as the baseline, enabling detection of any operator modification to this creditworthiness indicator.
3862 *First Name
3863 MOVE CUST-FIRST-NAME TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-FIRST-NAME Saves the customer's first name as the baseline for change detection against any operator edits.
3864 *Middle Name
3865 MOVE CUST-MIDDLE-NAME TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME Saves the customer's middle name as the baseline for change detection against any operator edits.
3866 *Last Name
3867 MOVE CUST-LAST-NAME TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-LAST-NAME Saves the customer's last name as the baseline for change detection against any operator edits.
3868 *Address
3869 MOVE CUST-ADDR-LINE-1 TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1 Saves the first line of the customer's mailing address as the baseline for change detection.
3870 MOVE CUST-ADDR-LINE-2 TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2 Saves the second line of the customer's mailing address as the baseline for change detection.
3871 MOVE CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 Saves the third line of the customer's mailing address as the baseline for change detection.
3872 MOVE CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD Saves the customer's US state code as the baseline for change detection.
3873 MOVE CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD TO Saves the customer's country code as the baseline for change detection.
3874 ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD
3875 MOVE CUST-ADDR-ZIP TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-ZIP Saves the customer's postal zip code as the baseline for change detection.
3876 MOVE CUST-PHONE-NUM-1 TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1 Saves the customer's primary contact phone number as the baseline for change detection.
3877 MOVE CUST-PHONE-NUM-2 TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2 Saves the customer's secondary contact phone number as the baseline for change detection.
3878 *Government Id
3879 MOVE CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID Saves the customer's government-issued identification number as the baseline for change detection.
3880 *EFT Code
3881 MOVE CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID Saves the customer's electronic funds transfer account identifier as the baseline for change detection.
3882 *Primary Holder Indicator
3883 MOVE CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND TO ACUP-OLD-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND Saves the indicator designating whether this customer is the primary cardholder on the account as the baseline for change detection.

3888 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING. Entry point for the database write phase of the account update transaction.
3889
3890 * Read the account file for update
3891
3892 MOVE CC-ACCT-ID TO WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID Prepares the account identifier to be used as the key for locating the account record in the master file.
3893
3894 EXEC CICS READ Locks the credit card account master record exclusively so no other operator can modify it simultaneously during this update.
3895 FILE (LIT-ACCTFILENAME)
3896 UPDATE
3897 RIDFLD (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X)
3898 KEYLENGTH (LENGTH OF WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X)
3899 INTO (ACCOUNT-RECORD)
3900 LENGTH (LENGTH OF ACCOUNT-RECORD)
3901 RESP (WS-RESP-CD)
3902 RESP2 (WS-REAS-CD)
3903 END-EXEC
3904 *****************************************************************
3905 * Could we lock the account record ?
3906 *****************************************************************
3907 IF WS-RESP-CD EQUAL TO DFHRESP(NORMAL) Checks whether the account record was successfully locked for exclusive update access.
3908 CONTINUE Lock succeeded — processing continues to the next step.
3909 ELSE
3910 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall transaction as failed due to a locking problem.
3911 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether an error message has already been set for the operator, to avoid overwriting a more specific earlier message.
3912 SET COULD-NOT-LOCK-ACCT-FOR-UPDATE TO TRUE Sets the operator-facing error message to indicate the account record could not be reserved for update, likely because another user holds it.
3913 END-IF
3914 GO TO 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT Abandons the write attempt and exits this section, returning control so the error can be reported to the operator.
3915 END-IF
3916
3917 * Read the customer file for update
3918
3919 MOVE CDEMO-CUST-ID TO WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID Prepares the customer identifier to be used as the key for locating the customer demographic record in the customer master file.
3920
3921 EXEC CICS READ Locks the customer demographic record exclusively so no other operator can modify it simultaneously during this update.
3922 FILE (LIT-CUSTFILENAME)
3923 UPDATE
3924 RIDFLD (WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X)
3925 KEYLENGTH (LENGTH OF WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X)
3926 INTO (CUSTOMER-RECORD)
3927 LENGTH (LENGTH OF CUSTOMER-RECORD)
3928 RESP (WS-RESP-CD)
3929 RESP2 (WS-REAS-CD)
3930 END-EXEC
3931 *****************************************************************
3932 * Could we lock the customer record ?
3933 *****************************************************************
3934 IF WS-RESP-CD EQUAL TO DFHRESP(NORMAL) Checks whether the customer record was successfully locked for exclusive update access.
3935 CONTINUE Lock succeeded — processing continues to the next step.
3936 ELSE
3937 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE Marks the overall transaction as failed due to a customer record locking problem.
3938 IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF Checks whether an error message has already been set, to avoid overwriting a more specific earlier message.
3939 SET COULD-NOT-LOCK-CUST-FOR-UPDATE TO TRUE Sets the operator-facing error message to indicate the customer record could not be reserved for update.
3940 END-IF
3941 GO TO 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT Abandons the write attempt and exits this section so the error can be reported to the operator.
3942 END-IF

3944 *****************************************************************
3945 * Did someone change the record while we were out ?
3946 *****************************************************************
3947 PERFORM 9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC Invokes a sub-routine that compares the currently locked record data against what was originally displayed to the operator, detecting any concurrent changes made by another user.
3948 THRU 9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC-EXIT
3949
3950 IF DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE Checks whether another user modified the account or customer data after the operator loaded the screen but before submitting the update.
3951 GO TO 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT If a concurrent modification is detected, abandons this update to prevent overwriting another operator's changes, exiting to report the conflict.
3952 END-IF

3954 * Prepare the update
3955 *****************************************************************

4061 * Update account *
4062 *****************************************************************
4063
4064
4065 EXEC CICS Writes the fully assembled account update record back to the credit card account master file, replacing the previously locked record with the new values.
4066 REWRITE FILE(LIT-ACCTFILENAME)
4067 FROM(ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD)
4068 LENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD)
4069 RESP (WS-RESP-CD)
4070 RESP2 (WS-REAS-CD)
4071 END-EXEC.
4072 *
4073 *****************************************************************
4074 * Did account update succeed ? *
4075 *****************************************************************
4076 IF WS-RESP-CD EQUAL TO DFHRESP(NORMAL) Checks whether the account master file write completed successfully.
4077 CONTINUE Account write succeeded — processing continues to update the customer record.
4078 ELSE
4079 SET LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED TO TRUE Marks the transaction as failed, indicating the account record was locked but the actual write to the database did not succeed.
4080 GO TO 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT Exits the write section so the failure can be reported to the operator.
4081 END-IF
4082 *****************************************************************
4083 * Update customer *
4084 *****************************************************************
4085 EXEC CICS Writes the fully assembled customer update record back to the customer master file, replacing the previously locked record with the new demographic values.
4086 REWRITE FILE(LIT-CUSTFILENAME)
4087 FROM(CUST-UPDATE-RECORD)
4088 LENGTH(LENGTH OF CUST-UPDATE-RECORD)
4089 RESP (WS-RESP-CD)
4090 RESP2 (WS-REAS-CD)
4091 END-EXEC.
4092 *****************************************************************
4093 * Did customer update succeed ? *
4094 *****************************************************************
4095 IF WS-RESP-CD EQUAL TO DFHRESP(NORMAL) Checks whether the customer master file write completed successfully.
4096 CONTINUE Customer write succeeded — both records have been updated and the transaction is complete.
4097 ELSE
4098 SET LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED TO TRUE Marks the transaction as failed, indicating the customer record was locked but the actual write to the database did not succeed.
4099 EXEC CICS Issues a full transaction rollback, reversing the previously committed account master file update to maintain data consistency between the two linked records.
4100 SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK
4101 END-EXEC
4102 GO TO 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT Exits the write section so the failure and rollback can be reported to the operator.

4112 ******************************************************************
4113 * Account Master data
4114 ******************************************************************
4115 IF ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS EQUAL ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS Begins comparing the account's active/inactive status as it exists in the database against the value originally displayed to the operator on screen.
4116 * Current Balance
4117 AND ACCT-CURR-BAL EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N Checks whether the current outstanding balance on the account has been altered from what was originally shown.
4118 * Credit Limit
4119 AND ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N Checks whether the total credit limit approved for the account has been changed from the original displayed value.
4120 * Cash Limit
4121 AND ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N Checks whether the cash advance credit limit has been changed from the original displayed value.
4122 * Current Cycle Credit
4123 AND ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N Checks whether the total credits posted to the account in the current billing cycle have been altered.
4124 * Current Cycle Debit
4125 AND ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N Checks whether the total debits posted to the account in the current billing cycle have been altered.
4126 * Open date
4127 AND ACCT-OPEN-DATE(1:4) EQUAL ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR Checks whether the year portion of the account opening date has been changed.
4128 AND ACCT-OPEN-DATE(6:2) EQUAL ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON Checks whether the month portion of the account opening date has been changed.
4129 AND ACCT-OPEN-DATE(9:2) EQUAL ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY Checks whether the day portion of the account opening date has been changed.
4130 * Expiry date
4131 AND ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE(1:4)EQUAL ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR Checks whether the year portion of the credit card expiry date has been changed.
4132 AND ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE(6:2)EQUAL ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON Checks whether the month portion of the credit card expiry date has been changed.
4133 AND ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE(9:2)EQUAL ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY Checks whether the day portion of the credit card expiry date has been changed.
4134 * Reissue date
4135 AND ACCT-REISSUE-DATE(1:4) EQUAL ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR Checks whether the year portion of the card reissue/renewal date has been changed.
4136 AND ACCT-REISSUE-DATE(6:2) EQUAL ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON Checks whether the month portion of the card reissue/renewal date has been changed.
4137 AND ACCT-REISSUE-DATE(9:2) EQUAL ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY Checks whether the day portion of the card reissue/renewal date has been changed.
4138 * Account Group
4139 AND FUNCTION LOWER-CASE (ACCT-GROUP-ID) EQUAL Checks whether the account group/portfolio classification code has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison to avoid false positives from capitalisation differences.
4140 FUNCTION LOWER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID) Completes the case-insensitive comparison of the account group code against the original value shown on screen.
4141 CONTINUE If all account financial fields are identical to their original values, no action is taken and processing continues to the customer data comparison below.
4142 ELSE If any single account financial field differs from its original value, the following action is triggered.
4143 SET DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE TO TRUE Marks the transaction as containing genuine data changes, authorising the subsequent database write operations to proceed.
4144 GO TO 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT Exits this routine immediately and routes control to the write-processing logic, since a change has already been confirmed and further comparison is unnecessary.
4145 END-IF Closes the account-data comparison block.

4147 ******************************************************************
4148 * Customer data - Split into 2 IFs for easier reading
4149 * And maybe put logic to update only 1 file if only date
4150 * pertaining to one of them is updated
4151 ******************************************************************
4152 IF FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-FIRST-NAME ) EQUAL Begins comparing the customer's first name against the original value, using case-insensitive matching to avoid treating a capitalisation change as a data modification.
4153 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-FIRST-NAME ) Completes the case-insensitive first name comparison against the original screen value.
4154 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME ) EQUAL Checks whether the customer's middle name has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4155 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME) Completes the case-insensitive middle name comparison against the original screen value.
4156 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-LAST-NAME ) EQUAL Checks whether the customer's last name has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4157 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-LAST-NAME ) Completes the case-insensitive last name comparison against the original screen value.
4158 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-ADDR-LINE-1 ) EQUAL Checks whether the first line of the customer's street address has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4159 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1) Completes the case-insensitive address line 1 comparison against the original screen value.
4160 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-ADDR-LINE-2 ) EQUAL Checks whether the second line of the customer's street address has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4161 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2) Completes the case-insensitive address line 2 comparison against the original screen value.
4162 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 ) EQUAL Checks whether the third line of the customer's address (typically city or locality) has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4163 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3) Completes the case-insensitive address line 3 comparison against the original screen value.
4164 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD ) EQUAL Checks whether the customer's US state code has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4165 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD) Completes the case-insensitive state code comparison against the original screen value.
4166 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD ) EQUAL Checks whether the customer's country code has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4167 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD ) Completes the case-insensitive country code comparison against the original screen value.
4168 AND CUST-ADDR-ZIP EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-ZIP Checks whether the customer's postal/ZIP code has been changed from the original value.
4169 AND CUST-PHONE-NUM-1 EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1 Checks whether the customer's primary telephone number has been changed from the original value.
4170 AND CUST-PHONE-NUM-2 EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2 Checks whether the customer's secondary telephone number has been changed from the original value.
4171 AND CUST-SSN EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CUST-SSN Checks whether the customer's Social Security Number has been changed from the original value.
4172 AND FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID ) EQUAL Checks whether the government-issued identification number (e.g. passport or driver's licence) has been changed, using case-insensitive comparison.
4173 FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (ACUP-OLD-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID ) Completes the case-insensitive government ID comparison against the original screen value.
4174 AND CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD (1:4) EQUAL Checks whether the year portion of the customer's date of birth has been changed.
4175 ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD (1:4) Completes the year-of-birth comparison against the original screen value.
4176 AND CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD (6:2) EQUAL Checks whether the month portion of the customer's date of birth has been changed.
4177 ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD (5:2) Completes the month-of-birth comparison against the original screen value.
4178 AND CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD (9:2) EQUAL Checks whether the day portion of the customer's date of birth has been changed.
4179 ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD (7:2) Completes the day-of-birth comparison against the original screen value.
4180
4181 AND CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID EQUAL Checks whether the customer's linked electronic funds transfer bank account identifier has been changed.
4182 ACUP-OLD-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID Completes the EFT account identifier comparison against the original screen value.
4183 AND CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND Checks whether the indicator designating this customer as the primary cardholder on the account has been changed.
4184 EQUAL
4185 ACUP-OLD-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND Completes the primary cardholder indicator comparison against the original screen value.
4186 AND CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE EQUAL ACUP-OLD-CUST-FICO-SCORE Checks whether the customer's FICO credit score has been changed from the original value.
4187 CONTINUE If all customer demographic fields are identical to their original values, no action is taken — the entire submission is confirmed as unchanged.
4188 ELSE If any single customer demographic field differs from its original value, the following action is triggered.
4189 SET DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE TO TRUE Marks the transaction as containing genuine data changes, authorising the subsequent database write operations to proceed.
4190 GO TO 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT Exits this routine immediately and routes control to the write-processing logic, since a customer data change has been confirmed.
4191 END-IF Closes the customer data comparison block and ends the paragraph.

4203 ABEND-ROUTINE. Entry point invoked whenever the account update program encounters a fatal, unrecoverable error condition.
4204
4205 IF ABEND-MSG EQUAL LOW-VALUES Checks whether a specific failure description was already captured earlier in the process, or whether the crash was entirely unexpected with no prior context.
4206 MOVE 'UNEXPECTED ABEND OCCURRED.' TO ABEND-MSG If no prior failure description exists, stamps the incident record with a generic message indicating an unexpected system crash occurred during the account update.
4207 END-IF
4208
4209 MOVE LIT-THISPGM TO ABEND-CULPRIT Records the identity of this account update program as the source of the failure, so support staff know exactly which program abended.
4210
4211 EXEC CICS SEND Transmits the failure details — including the program identity and error description — directly to the operator's terminal screen, ensuring staff are immediately informed of the crash.
4212 FROM (ABEND-DATA)
4213 LENGTH(LENGTH OF ABEND-DATA)
4214 NOHANDLE
4215 ERASE
4216 END-EXEC
4217
4218 EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND Cancels any previously registered automatic recovery handlers, preventing the system from attempting an uncontrolled or partial recovery that could leave account data in an inconsistent state.
4219 CANCEL
4220 END-EXEC
4221
4222 EXEC CICS ABEND Formally terminates the transaction with a standardised failure code (9999), signalling to CICS and operations monitoring tools that this account update ended in a critical unrecoverable error requiring investigation.
4223 ABCODE('9999')
4224 END-EXEC
4225 .
4226 ABEND-ROUTINE-EXIT. Marks the end boundary of the abnormal-termination handling routine — the designated landing point after all abend recovery steps have completed.
4227 EXIT Formally exits the abend-handling routine, returning control to the CICS transaction manager with no further processing — the program terminates cleanly after any critical failure.

Variables & Data Structures
Level Name PIC Value Description
01 WS-MISC-STORAGE
Group field 		– – Top-level working storage container grouping all miscellaneous operational variables used during account update processing, including CICS communication variables and field validation scratch areas.
05 WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
Group field 		– – Group of variables used to communicate with the CICS transaction processing environment — captures system responses when reading or writing account and customer records, and identifies the current transaction being executed.
07 WS-RESP-CD PIC S9(09) COMP – CICS response code returned after every file read or write operation (e.g. reading the account master record or writing updated customer data). A non-zero value signals that the database operation failed, triggering error handling to prevent corrupt or partial updates to the account or customer record.
07 WS-REAS-CD PIC S9(09) COMP – CICS reason code that supplements the response code to provide more specific detail about why a file I/O operation failed — for example, distinguishing between a record-not-found condition versus a file unavailable condition when retrieving account or customer records.
07 WS-TRANID PIC X(4) – The four-character CICS transaction identifier for the account update program. This identifies which transaction the bank operator is currently executing, used for routing and audit purposes within the CardDemo system.
07 WS-UCTRANS PIC X(4) – Uppercase version of the transaction identifier. Used to normalize the transaction ID to uppercase before comparison or display, ensuring consistent identification of the account update transaction regardless of how the operator entered it.
05 WS-GENERIC-EDITS
Group field 		– – Group of reusable scratch-pad variables used during field-by-field validation of account and customer data entered on the update screen. These variables are loaded with each field's value in turn and then inspected by shared validation routines before the update is committed.
10 WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME PIC X(25) – Holds the human-readable name of the field currently being validated (e.g. 'CREDIT LIMIT' or 'DATE OF BIRTH'). Used to construct meaningful error messages that tell the bank operator exactly which field on the account update screen contains invalid data.
10 WS-EDIT-SIGNED-NUMBER-9V2-X PIC X(15) – Scratch area holding the raw text representation of a monetary amount entered by the bank operator (such as credit limit, cash credit limit, current balance, or cycle credits/debits) before it is validated as a properly signed numeric dollar-and-cents value.
10 WS-FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-EDIT PIC X(1) – Validation result flag for a monetary amount field (credit limit, balance, cycle amounts, etc.). Indicates whether the value entered by the bank operator is a valid signed numeric amount, is invalid, or was left blank — controlling whether the update is allowed to proceed.
88 FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the monetary amount entered (e.g. credit limit or current balance) has passed numeric format validation and is acceptable for saving to the account master record.
88 FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that the monetary amount entered by the bank operator is not a valid signed numeric value — for example, contains letters or an invalid sign — and the update must be rejected with an error message.
88 FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating that a required monetary amount field (such as credit limit or current balance) was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error distinct from a format error.
10 WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY PIC X(256) – Scratch buffer holding the text value of an address or other alphanumeric field entered by the bank operator (street address, city, state, zip, country) while it is being checked to ensure it contains only valid alphanumeric characters before being saved to the customer record.
10 WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH PIC S9(4) COMP-3 – The length of the alphanumeric field currently being validated. Used by the shared validation routine to know how many characters of the address or other text field to inspect, since different fields (street line 1, city, zip, etc.) have different maximum lengths.
10 WS-EDIT-ALPHA-ONLY-FLAGS PIC X(1) – Validation result flag for fields that must contain alphabetic characters only, such as customer first name, middle name, and last name. Indicates whether the name entered by the bank operator is valid, invalid, or blank.
88 FLG-ALPHA-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that a customer name field (first, middle, or last name) contains only alphabetic characters and has passed validation, allowing the update to proceed.
88 FLG-ALPHA-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that a customer name field contains non-alphabetic characters (such as digits or special characters), which violates the business rule that names must be alphabetic only — the update will be rejected.
88 FLG-ALPHA-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating that a required customer name field was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error so the operator knows which name field must be filled in.
10 WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY-FLAGS PIC X(1) – Validation result flag for fields that must contain alphanumeric characters only, such as address lines, city, state, zip code, and country. Indicates whether the value entered by the bank operator is valid, invalid, or blank.
88 FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that a customer address field contains only valid alphanumeric characters and has passed validation, allowing the customer record update to proceed.
88 FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that a customer address field contains invalid characters (e.g. special characters not permitted in an address), causing the update to be rejected with an appropriate error message.
88 FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating that a required customer address field was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error distinct from a format validation error.
10 WS-EDIT-MANDATORY-FLAGS PIC X(1) – General-purpose mandatory field validation flag used to enforce that required fields on the account update screen have been filled in by the bank operator before the update is allowed to proceed.
88 FLG-MANDATORY-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that a mandatory field has been populated by the bank operator and satisfies the presence requirement, allowing validation to continue to format checks.
88 FLG-MANDATORY-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that a mandatory field on the account update screen has been provided but contains an invalid value, requiring the bank operator to correct it before the update can be saved.
88 FLG-MANDATORY-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating that a mandatory field was left completely blank by the bank operator — a distinct error from an invalid value — prompting the operator to supply the missing required information.
10 WS-EDIT-YES-NO PIC X(1) – Scratch field holding the value entered by the bank operator for a Yes/No field, most critically the account active/inactive status flag. Used to validate that only 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive) has been entered, as required by business rules.
88 FLG-YES-NO-ISVALID – 'Y', 'N' Condition indicating that the account status field contains a valid value — either 'Y' for active or 'N' for inactive — satisfying the business rule that no other values are permitted for account status.
88 FLG-YES-NO-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that the account status field contains an invalid value (neither 'Y' nor 'N'), causing the update to be rejected and the bank operator to be prompted to enter a valid status.
88 FLG-YES-NO-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating that the account status field was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error since account status is required and must be explicitly set to active or inactive.
10 WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUM PIC X(15) – The customer's US telephone number as entered by the bank operator on the update screen, stored as a 15-character string in the format NXX-NXX-XXXX before being broken into its three segments (area code, exchange, subscriber number) for individual validation.
10 WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUM-X
Group field

88 FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEB-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the phone number exchange segment entered by the bank operator is numeric and has passed validation, satisfying the second segment of US phone number format requirements.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEB-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that the phone number exchange segment entered by the bank operator is not valid (e.g. contains non-numeric characters), requiring correction before the customer record can be updated.

88 FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEC-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that the four-digit subscriber number segment of the customer's phone number is invalid (e.g. contains non-numeric characters), requiring the bank operator to correct it.

Group field
REDEFINES WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2 		– – Numeric reinterpretation of the middle 2-digit segment of the customer's Social Security Number, enabling the program to perform numeric validity checks (non-zero, all digits) on this portion of the SSN.
20 WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3 PIC X(4) – The last 4-digit serial number segment of the customer's Social Security Number as entered by the bank operator. This segment is validated independently to confirm it is numeric and non-zero, ensuring the SSN on the customer record is genuine and complete.

Group field
REDEFINES WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3 		– – Numeric reinterpretation of the last 4-digit segment of the customer's Social Security Number, allowing numeric validation checks (non-zero, all digits) to be applied to this portion of the SSN before the customer record is updated.

Group field
REDEFINES WS-EDIT-US-SSN 		– – Numeric reinterpretation of the entire Social Security Number field, providing a combined numeric view of all three SSN segments to support whole-SSN numeric validation checks during the customer record update process.

88 WS-EDIT-US-SSN-IS-INVALID – '000' Condition that is true when all three segments of the customer's SSN have failed validation (all flags set to '0'). When this condition is met, the entire SSN is considered invalid and the account update is blocked until the operator corrects the SSN.
88 WS-EDIT-US-SSN-IS-VALID – LOW-VALUES Condition that is true when all three segments of the customer's SSN have passed validation (all flags are clear/LOW-VALUES). This is the green-light condition that allows the SSN portion of the customer update to proceed to the database write.
20 WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the first 3-digit segment of the customer's SSN. It records whether this segment passed validation, was found to be in an invalid format or prohibited range, or was left blank by the operator — enabling targeted error feedback on the update screen.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the first 3-digit SSN segment is valid — it is numeric, non-zero, and not a prohibited value (not 000, 666, or 900-999). The update can proceed for this SSN segment.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the first 3-digit SSN segment contains an invalid value — either non-numeric or a prohibited SSN prefix (000, 666, 900-999). The operator must correct this segment before the customer record can be updated.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the first SSN segment blank on the update screen. Since SSN is a mandatory customer identity field, a blank entry is treated as a distinct error requiring the operator to supply the missing information.
20 WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the middle 2-digit group segment of the customer's SSN. Tracks whether this segment is valid, invalid, or blank, enabling the program to provide specific error guidance to the bank operator.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the middle 2-digit SSN group number is valid — numeric and non-zero. This segment of the SSN has passed its validation check and does not block the customer record update.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the middle 2-digit SSN segment is invalid (non-numeric or zero). The operator must correct this value before the customer record update can be saved to the database.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the middle SSN segment blank. As a mandatory identity field, the missing group number must be supplied before the customer record update is accepted.
20 WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the last 4-digit serial segment of the customer's SSN. Records whether this segment is valid, invalid, or blank, supporting precise error messaging on the account update screen.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the last 4-digit SSN serial number is valid — numeric and non-zero. This segment has passed validation and does not prevent the customer record from being updated.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the last 4-digit SSN segment is invalid (non-numeric or zero). The operator must provide a correct serial number before the customer record update can be committed.
88 FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the last SSN segment blank on the screen. The 4-digit serial number is mandatory for customer identity verification and must be entered before the update is accepted.
05 WS-CALCULATION-VARS
Group field 		– – Group of working variables used for arithmetic calculations during the account update process, such as date validation arithmetic and any numeric range checks performed on financial or date fields.
10 WS-DIV-BY PIC S9(4) COMP-3 – The divisor used in arithmetic calculations during validation — for example, when checking whether a date component (such as a day value) falls within a valid range by performing division or modulo operations.
10 WS-DIVIDEND PIC S9(4) COMP-3 – The value being divided during arithmetic validation calculations — for example, a date component or numeric field value being tested for validity through division.
10 WS-REMAINDER PIC S9(4) COMP-3 – The remainder produced by a division calculation during validation — used, for example, to determine whether a year is a leap year when validating date fields such as date of birth, account open date, or card expiry date.
10 WS-CURR-DATE PIC X(21) – The current system date and time at the moment the bank operator submits the update. Used as the reference point for date-range validations — for example, ensuring the card expiry date is in the future and the customer's date of birth is in the past.
05 WS-DATACHANGED-FLAG PIC X(1) – Tracks whether the bank operator has actually modified any field on the account update screen. Prevents unnecessary and potentially disruptive database writes when the operator submits the screen without making any changes.
88 NO-CHANGES-FOUND – '0' Condition indicating that the operator submitted the update screen without changing any data. When true, the program skips the database write and informs the operator that no update was necessary.
88 CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED – '1' Condition indicating that at least one field on the account update screen has been modified by the operator. When true, the program proceeds to validate and then write the changes to the account and customer database records.
05 WS-INPUT-FLAG PIC X(1) – Overall result of all input validation checks on the update screen. Acts as the master gate — only when all individual field validations pass (INPUT-OK) is the program allowed to write the updated account and customer data to the database.
88 INPUT-OK – '0' Condition indicating that all fields on the account update screen have passed validation. This is the green-light condition that authorises the program to save the updated account and customer information to the database.
88 INPUT-ERROR – '1' Condition indicating that one or more fields on the account update screen have failed validation. The database update is blocked and the operator is returned to the screen with error messages highlighting the fields that need correction.
88 INPUT-PENDING – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that input validation has not yet been performed — typically the initial state when the screen is first displayed to the operator before any data has been submitted for validation.
05 WS-RETURN-FLAG PIC X(1) – Controls whether the program should return control to the calling menu or parent program after completing (or cancelling) the account update. Governs the navigation flow between the update screen and the rest of the CardDemo application.
88 WS-RETURN-FLAG-OFF – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the program should remain on the account update screen — the operator has not yet completed or cancelled the update, so control stays within this program.
88 WS-RETURN-FLAG-ON – '1' Condition indicating the program should transfer control back to the calling menu or parent program — typically set after a successful update, a cancellation by the operator, or a fatal error that cannot be resolved on this screen.
05 WS-PFK-FLAG PIC X(1) – Records whether the bank operator pressed a recognised and permitted function key (such as Enter to submit or PF3 to cancel). Prevents the program from processing the screen when an unsupported key is pressed.
88 PFK-VALID – '0' Condition indicating the operator pressed a valid, supported function key. The program will proceed to process the screen input according to the key pressed (e.g. submit update, cancel, return to menu).
88 PFK-INVALID – '1' Condition indicating the operator pressed an unrecognised or unsupported function key. The program will display an error message and redisplay the screen without processing any data, prompting the operator to use a valid key.
05 WS-EDIT-ACCT-FLAG PIC X(1) – Validation result for the account number entered on the update screen. Indicates whether the account number is valid and exists in the system, invalid in format, or was left blank — determining whether the account record can be retrieved and updated.
88 FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID – '1' Condition indicating the account number entered by the operator is valid and the corresponding account record was successfully found in the system. The program can proceed to display and update the account details.
88 FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the account number entered is invalid — either it does not exist in the system or it fails format validation. The operator must supply a correct account number before the update can proceed.
88 FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK – ' ' Condition indicating the operator left the account number field blank on the update screen. Since the account number is the primary key for retrieving the record to be updated, it is mandatory and must be provided.
05 WS-EDIT-CUST-FLAG PIC X(1) – Validation result for the customer number entered on the update screen. Indicates whether the customer number is valid and matches a customer record linked to the account, is invalid, or was left blank — controlling whether the customer demographic data can be updated.
88 FLG-CUSTFILTER-ISVALID – '1' Condition indicating the customer number entered by the operator is valid and the corresponding customer record was found in the system. The program can proceed to display and update the customer's demographic information.
88 FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the customer number entered is invalid — either it does not exist or fails format validation. The operator must provide a valid customer number before the customer record update can proceed.
88 FLG-CUSTFILTER-BLANK – ' ' Condition indicating the operator left the customer number field blank. The customer number is required to identify which customer record to update alongside the account record, so it must be supplied.
05 WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS
Group field 		– – Group of validation status flags for all non-key data fields on the account update screen (such as account status, credit limits, balances, dates, and customer details). Each flag records the validation outcome for its respective field, collectively determining whether the update can be saved.
10 WS-EDIT-ACCT-STATUS PIC X(1) – Validation status flag for the account active/inactive status field. Records whether the operator entered a valid status value (Y for active or N for inactive), an invalid value, or left the field blank — enforcing the business rule that only Y or N are permitted.
88 FLG-ACCT-STATUS-ISVALID – 'Y', 'N' Condition indicating the account status field contains a valid value — either Y (account is active and can be used for transactions) or N (account is inactive and blocked from use). The update can proceed for this field.
88 FLG-ACCT-STATUS-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the account status field contains an invalid value — something other than Y or N. The operator must correct this to either Y (active) or N (inactive) before the account record can be updated.
88 FLG-ACCT-STATUS-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the account status field blank. Account status is a mandatory field — the operator must explicitly set the account to active (Y) or inactive (N) before the update is accepted.
10 WS-EDIT-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC X(1) – Validation status flag for the account's total credit limit field. Records whether the credit limit amount entered by the operator is a valid signed numeric value, is in an invalid format, or was left blank — controlling whether this financial limit can be updated on the account record.
88 FLG-CRED-LIMIT-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the credit limit amount entered is a valid signed numeric value. The maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to charge to this account has passed validation and can be saved to the account master record.
88 FLG-CRED-LIMIT-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the credit limit amount entered is invalid — for example, contains non-numeric characters or is in an unacceptable format. The operator must correct the credit limit before the account record can be updated.
88 FLG-CRED-LIMIT-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the credit limit field blank. The credit limit is a mandatory financial control field on the account — it must be provided to define the maximum borrowing capacity for the cardholder.
10 WS-EDIT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC X(1) – Validation status flag for the account's cash advance credit limit field. Records whether the cash advance limit entered by the operator is a valid signed numeric value, is invalid, or was left blank — this limit controls the maximum cash the cardholder can withdraw against the account.
88 FLG-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the cash advance credit limit entered is a valid signed numeric value. The maximum amount the cardholder can withdraw as cash against this account has passed validation and can be saved to the account master record.
88 FLG-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the cash advance credit limit entered is invalid — for example, non-numeric or incorrectly formatted. The operator must supply a valid cash advance limit before the account record update can be committed to the database.
88 FLG-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-BLANK – B Condition flag indicating that the bank staff left the cash advance credit limit field completely empty on the update screen. A blank mandatory field is treated as a distinct error from an invalid value — the operator must supply a cash credit limit before the account update can be saved.
10 WS-EDIT-CURR-BAL PIC X(1) – Validation status flag for the customer's current outstanding account balance entered on the update screen. Holds one of three states: valid (LOW-VALUES), invalid format ('0'), or left blank ('B'). The update cannot proceed to the database if this flag is not in the valid state, ensuring the account balance on record is always a legitimate signed numeric amount.
88 FLG-CURR-BAL-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the current outstanding balance entered by the bank operator has passed all format and numeric validation checks and is acceptable for saving to the account master record.
88 FLG-CURR-BAL-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the current outstanding balance entered on screen contains an invalid value — for example, non-numeric characters or an improperly formatted signed amount. The operator will be shown an error and must correct the balance before the account record can be updated.
88 FLG-CURR-BAL-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the current outstanding balance field empty on the update screen. Since a balance is required for a valid account record, this blank condition triggers a specific error message distinct from an invalid-format error.
10 WS-EDIT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT PIC X(1) – Validation status flag for the total credit transactions posted to the account during the current billing cycle. Ensures that payments, refunds, and other credits entered by the operator are a valid signed numeric amount before being written to the account master record.
88 FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the current billing cycle credit amount has passed validation and is ready to be saved to the account record.
88 FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the current billing cycle credit amount entered on screen is not a valid numeric value. The operator must correct this field before the account update can be committed.
88 FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the current billing cycle credit field blank. This is flagged separately from an invalid value so the operator receives a clear message that the field must be populated.
10 WS-EDIT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT PIC X(1) – Validation status flag for the total debit transactions (purchases, fees, charges) posted to the account during the current billing cycle. Prevents invalid or missing debit cycle amounts from being written to the account master record.
88 FLG-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the current billing cycle debit amount has passed all validation checks and is acceptable for saving to the account record.
88 FLG-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the current billing cycle debit amount entered on screen is not a valid numeric value. The account update will be blocked until the operator corrects this field.
88 FLG-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the current billing cycle debit field blank on the update screen, triggering a specific 'field required' error message.
10 WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-FLGS
Group field 		– – Composite validation record for the customer's date of birth entered on the update screen. Groups three individual component flags (year, month, day) so the program can validate each part of the birth date independently and report precisely which component is missing or invalid. A valid birth date is required to correctly identify the customer and maintain accurate demographic records.
88 WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-INVALID – 000 Condition indicating that all three components of the customer's date of birth (year, month, and day) have failed validation simultaneously. When this fires, the entire birth date is rejected and the operator must re-enter a valid calendar date.
88 WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the customer's complete date of birth — year, month, and day — has passed all validation checks and is a legitimate calendar date acceptable for saving to the customer master record.
20 WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-FLG PIC X(01) – Validation status flag specifically for the year component of the customer's date of birth. Ensures the birth year entered is a valid numeric value and falls within an acceptable range (i.e., represents a plausible birth year for a living customer).
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the year portion of the customer's date of birth is a valid numeric year and has passed all range checks.
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the year portion of the customer's date of birth is not a valid numeric value or falls outside an acceptable range. The operator must correct the birth year before the customer record can be updated.
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the birth year field empty. A missing birth year is flagged distinctly so the operator receives a clear 'field required' message rather than a generic format error.
20 WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH PIC X(01) – Validation status flag specifically for the month component of the customer's date of birth. Ensures the entered month is numeric and falls between 01 and 12, representing a real calendar month.
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the month portion of the customer's date of birth is a valid calendar month (01–12) and has passed all validation checks.
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the month portion of the customer's date of birth is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a month number outside the range 01–12.
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the birth month field blank on the update screen, requiring a specific 'field required' error to be displayed.
20 WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY PIC X(01) – Validation status flag specifically for the day component of the customer's date of birth. Ensures the entered day is numeric and valid for the given month and year (e.g., no 31st in April, no 29th of February in a non-leap year).
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the day portion of the customer's date of birth is a valid calendar day for the specified month and year.
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the day portion of the customer's date of birth is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a day that does not exist in the specified month.
88 FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the birth day field blank, triggering a 'field required' error message so the operator knows exactly which part of the date of birth is missing.
10 WS-EDIT-FICO-SCORE-FLGS PIC X(1) – Validation status flag for the customer's FICO credit score entered on the update screen. The FICO score is a key creditworthiness indicator used in lending decisions; this flag ensures the value entered is a valid numeric score within the accepted range (typically 300–850) before it is saved to the customer master record.
88 FLG-FICO-SCORE-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the FICO credit score entered by the operator is a valid numeric value within the acceptable range and can be saved to the customer record.
88 FLG-FICO-SCORE-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the FICO credit score entered on screen is not a valid numeric value or falls outside the acceptable score range. The operator must correct the score before the customer record can be updated.
88 FLG-FICO-SCORE-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the FICO score field blank on the update screen. Since the FICO score is required for credit risk assessment, this triggers a specific 'field required' error.
10 WS-EDIT-OPEN-DATE-FLGS
Group field 		– – Composite validation record for the account opening date entered on the update screen. Groups three individual component flags (year, month, day) so the program can pinpoint exactly which part of the account open date is missing or invalid. The account open date is a key audit and regulatory field that records when the credit card account was established.
88 WS-EDIT-OPEN-DATE-IS-INVALID – 000 Condition indicating that all three components of the account opening date (year, month, and day) have simultaneously failed validation. The entire open date is rejected and the operator must re-enter a valid calendar date.
20 WS-EDIT-OPEN-YEAR-FLG PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the year component of the account opening date. Ensures the year entered is numeric and represents a plausible year for when a credit card account could have been opened.
88 FLG-OPEN-YEAR-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the year portion of the account opening date is valid and acceptable for saving to the account master record.
88 FLG-OPEN-YEAR-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the year portion of the account opening date is not a valid numeric value or is outside an acceptable range. The operator must correct the open year before the account record can be updated.
88 FLG-OPEN-YEAR-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the account open year field blank, triggering a 'field required' error so the operator knows the year component of the open date must be supplied.
20 WS-EDIT-OPEN-MONTH PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the month component of the account opening date. Ensures the entered month is numeric and represents a valid calendar month (01–12).
88 FLG-OPEN-MONTH-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the month portion of the account opening date is a valid calendar month and has passed all validation checks.
88 FLG-OPEN-MONTH-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the month portion of the account opening date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a month number outside 01–12.
88 FLG-OPEN-MONTH-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the account open month field blank, requiring a specific 'field required' error message to be displayed.
20 WS-EDIT-OPEN-DAY PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the day component of the account opening date. Ensures the entered day is numeric and valid for the given month and year combination.
88 FLG-OPEN-DAY-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the day portion of the account opening date is a valid calendar day for the specified month and year.
88 FLG-OPEN-DAY-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the day portion of the account opening date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a day that does not exist in the specified month.
88 FLG-OPEN-DAY-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the account open day field blank, triggering a 'field required' error so the operator knows exactly which part of the open date is missing.
10 WS-EXPIRY-DATE-FLGS
Group field 		– – Composite validation record for the credit card expiry date entered on the update screen. Groups three individual component flags (year, month, day) to allow precise identification of which part of the expiry date is missing or invalid. The expiry date determines when the physical card ceases to be valid for transactions and drives card reissuance processes.
88 WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-IS-INVALID – 000 Condition indicating that all three components of the card expiry date (year, month, and day) have simultaneously failed validation. The entire expiry date is rejected and the operator must re-enter a valid future calendar date.
20 WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR-FLG PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the year component of the credit card expiry date. Ensures the expiry year is numeric and represents a future year, confirming the card has not already expired at the time of the update.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-YEAR-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the year portion of the card expiry date is valid and represents an acceptable future year for card validity.
