88 FLG-EXPIRY-YEAR-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the year portion of the card expiry date is not a valid numeric value or represents an unacceptable year (e.g., already in the past). The operator must correct the expiry year before the card record can be updated.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-YEAR-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the card expiry year field blank. Since an expiry date is mandatory for every credit card, this triggers a specific 'field required' error.
20 WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-MONTH PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the month component of the credit card expiry date. Ensures the entered expiry month is numeric and falls within the valid range of 01–12.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-MONTH-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the month portion of the card expiry date is a valid calendar month and has passed all validation checks.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-MONTH-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the month portion of the card expiry date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a month number outside 01–12. The operator must correct this before the card record can be saved.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-MONTH-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the card expiry month field blank, triggering a 'field required' error message.
20 WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-DAY PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the day component of the credit card expiry date. Ensures the entered expiry day is numeric and valid for the given expiry month and year.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-DAY-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating that the day portion of the card expiry date is a valid calendar day for the specified expiry month and year.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-DAY-NOT-OK – 0 Condition indicating that the day portion of the card expiry date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a day that does not exist in the specified expiry month. The operator must correct this before the card record can be updated.
88 FLG-EXPIRY-DAY-BLANK – B Condition indicating that the bank operator left the card expiry day field blank, triggering a specific 'field required' error so the operator knows exactly which component of the expiry date is missing.
10 WS-EDIT-REISSUE-DATE-FLGS
Group field 		– – Composite validation result for the card reissue/renewal date entered by the bank operator. Groups together the individual year, month, and day validation outcomes so the program can determine in one check whether the entire reissue date is acceptable before saving the card record.
88 WS-EDIT-REISSUE-DATE-INVALID – '000' Condition that is true when all three components of the card reissue date (year, month, and day) have each been individually flagged as invalid. When this fires, the entire reissue date is rejected and the operator must correct all three parts before the card renewal record can be saved.
20 WS-EDIT-REISSUE-YEAR-FLG PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the year portion of the card reissue/renewal date. Holds the outcome of checking whether the year entered by the operator is a plausible calendar year for a card renewal event.
88 FLG-REISSUE-YEAR-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the reissue year passed all validation checks and is an acceptable calendar year for a card renewal. When true, the year portion will not block the update from proceeding.
88 FLG-REISSUE-YEAR-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the reissue year entered by the operator failed validation — for example, an out-of-range or non-numeric year. The update will be blocked and the operator must correct the year before the card renewal date can be saved.
88 FLG-REISSUE-YEAR-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the reissue year field empty on the update screen. This is treated as a distinct error from an invalid value, allowing the program to display a specific 'field is required' message rather than a generic format error.
20 WS-EDIT-REISSUE-MONTH PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the month portion of the card reissue/renewal date. Records whether the month entered (01–12) is a valid calendar month for the card renewal event.
88 FLG-REISSUE-MONTH-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the reissue month passed validation and represents a real calendar month. When true, the month portion will not prevent the card renewal record from being saved.
88 FLG-REISSUE-MONTH-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the reissue month entered by the operator is invalid — for example, a value outside 01–12 or a non-numeric entry. The update is blocked until the operator provides a valid month.
88 FLG-REISSUE-MONTH-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the reissue month field blank on the screen. Treated separately from an invalid value so the program can prompt the operator specifically that the month is missing.
20 WS-EDIT-REISSUE-DAY PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the day portion of the card reissue/renewal date. Records whether the day entered is valid for the given month and year of the card renewal.
88 FLG-REISSUE-DAY-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the reissue day passed validation and is a legitimate calendar day within the specified month. When true, the day portion will not block saving the card renewal record.
88 FLG-REISSUE-DAY-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the reissue day entered by the operator is invalid — for example, day 31 in a 30-day month, or a non-numeric entry. The update is blocked until a valid day is provided.
88 FLG-REISSUE-DAY-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the reissue day field blank. Treated as a distinct missing-field error so the program can tell the operator specifically that the day of the reissue date must be entered.
10 WS-EDIT-NAME-FLAGS
Group field 		– – Composite validation result group for the customer's full name as entered on the update screen. Groups the individual first, middle, and last name validation flags so the program can assess overall name validity before writing the customer demographic record.
20 WS-EDIT-FIRST-NAME-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the customer's first name. Records whether the first name entered by the operator contains only alphabetic characters as required by business rules, or whether it is blank or contains invalid characters.
88 FLG-FIRST-NAME-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the customer's first name passed validation — it contains only alphabetic characters and is not blank. When true, the first name will not prevent the customer record from being updated.
88 FLG-FIRST-NAME-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the customer's first name contains invalid characters (e.g., digits or special characters). The update is blocked and the operator must correct the first name to contain alphabetic characters only.
88 FLG-FIRST-NAME-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the customer first name field empty. Since a customer must have a first name on record, this triggers a mandatory-field error distinct from a format error.
20 WS-EDIT-MIDDLE-NAME-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the customer's middle name. Records whether the middle name entered contains only alphabetic characters, is blank, or contains invalid characters.
88 FLG-MIDDLE-NAME-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the customer's middle name passed validation. When true, the middle name field will not block the customer record update from proceeding.
88 FLG-MIDDLE-NAME-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the customer's middle name contains invalid characters such as digits or punctuation. The operator must correct the middle name before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-MIDDLE-NAME-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the customer's middle name field was left blank by the operator. Depending on whether middle name is mandatory, this may trigger a required-field warning or be treated as an acceptable omission.
20 WS-EDIT-LAST-NAME-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the customer's last name (surname). Records whether the last name entered by the operator is alphabetic, blank, or contains invalid characters.
88 FLG-LAST-NAME-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the customer's last name passed validation and contains only alphabetic characters. When true, the last name will not prevent the customer demographic record from being updated.
88 FLG-LAST-NAME-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the customer's last name contains invalid characters. The update is blocked and the operator must supply a properly formatted surname before the record can be saved.
88 FLG-LAST-NAME-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the customer last name field empty. A customer's surname is a mandatory identifier, so this triggers a required-field error that must be resolved before the update can proceed.
10 WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-FLAGS
Group field 		– – Composite validation result group for all components of the customer's mailing address entered on the update screen. Groups street lines, city, state, zip code, country, and phone number flags so the program can assess the overall validity of the customer's contact address before writing the customer record.
20 WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-LINE-1-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the first line of the customer's street address (e.g., house number and street name). Records whether the value entered is alphanumeric, blank, or contains disallowed characters.
88 FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the first address line passed validation and contains acceptable alphanumeric content. When true, this field will not block the customer address update.
88 FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the first address line contains invalid characters. The operator must correct the street address entry before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the first address line blank. Since a primary street address is required for the customer record, this triggers a mandatory-field error.
20 WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-LINE-2-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the second line of the customer's street address (e.g., apartment, suite, or unit number). Records whether the optional secondary address line is valid, blank, or contains disallowed characters.
88 FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-2-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the second address line passed validation. When true, this field will not prevent the customer address from being updated.
88 FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-2-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the second address line contains invalid characters. The operator must correct the entry before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-2-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the second address line was left blank by the operator. As this is typically an optional field, a blank value may be acceptable and handled differently from a blank mandatory field.
20 WS-EDIT-CITY-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the city component of the customer's mailing address. Records whether the city name entered by the operator is valid, blank, or contains disallowed characters.
88 FLG-CITY-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the city name passed validation. When true, the city field will not block the customer address update from proceeding.
88 FLG-CITY-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the city name entered contains invalid characters. The operator must supply a valid city name before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-CITY-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the city field blank. City is a required address component, so this triggers a mandatory-field error that must be resolved before the update proceeds.
20 WS-EDIT-STATE-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the US state code in the customer's mailing address. Records whether the two-letter state abbreviation entered by the operator is a recognized US state code, blank, or invalid.
88 FLG-STATE-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the state code passed validation against the recognized list of US state abbreviations. When true, the state field will not prevent the customer address from being updated.
88 FLG-STATE-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the state code entered is not a valid US state abbreviation. The operator must correct the state before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-STATE-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the state field blank. State is a required address component for US customers, so this triggers a mandatory-field error.
20 WS-EDIT-ZIPCODE-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the postal ZIP code in the customer's mailing address. Records whether the ZIP code entered by the operator is numeric and in an acceptable format, blank, or invalid.
88 FLG-ZIPCODE-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the ZIP code passed validation. When true, the ZIP code field will not block the customer address update.
88 FLG-ZIPCODE-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the ZIP code entered is invalid — for example, contains non-numeric characters or is in an unrecognized format. The operator must correct the ZIP code before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-ZIPCODE-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the ZIP code field blank. ZIP code is a required address component, so this triggers a mandatory-field error that must be resolved before the update proceeds.
20 WS-EDIT-COUNTRY-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the country code in the customer's mailing address. Records whether the country value entered by the operator is a recognized alphanumeric country code, blank, or contains invalid characters.
88 FLG-COUNTRY-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the country code passed validation. When true, the country field will not prevent the customer address record from being updated.
88 FLG-COUNTRY-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the country code entered is invalid or unrecognized. The operator must supply a valid country code before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-COUNTRY-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the country field blank. If country is a required address component, this triggers a mandatory-field error.
20 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1-FLGS
Group field 		– – Composite validation result group for the customer's primary US phone number. Groups the individual segment flags (area code and exchange) so the program can determine whether the entire phone number is valid before saving the customer contact record.
88 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1-IS-INVALID – – Condition indicating that at least one segment of the customer's primary phone number failed validation — meaning the overall phone number is unacceptable. The operator must correct the phone number before the customer record can be saved.
30 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1A-FLG PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the area code segment (first three digits) of the customer's primary US phone number. Records whether the area code is a recognized North American Numbering Plan area code, blank, or invalid.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1A-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the phone area code passed validation against the list of recognized North American area codes. When true, the area code segment will not block the customer record update.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1A-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the phone area code entered is not a valid North American area code. The operator must correct the area code before the customer contact information can be saved.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1A-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the phone area code segment blank. Since a complete phone number is required, this triggers a mandatory-field error for the area code portion.
30 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1B PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the exchange segment (middle three digits, NXX) of the customer's primary US phone number. Records whether this segment is numeric and conforms to the expected phone number format.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition indicating the phone exchange segment passed validation and is a properly formatted numeric value. When true, this segment will not prevent the customer phone number from being accepted.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-NOT-OK – '0' Condition indicating the phone exchange segment entered is invalid — for example, contains non-numeric characters. The operator must correct this portion of the phone number before the customer record can be saved.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-BLANK – 'B' Condition indicating the operator left the phone exchange segment blank. Since a complete phone number requires all segments, this triggers a mandatory-field error for the exchange portion of the primary phone number.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-NOT-OK – '0' Condition flag indicating that the second digit segment of the customer's phone area code failed validation — the bank operator must correct this portion before the update can be saved.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-BLANK – 'B' Condition flag indicating that the second digit segment of the customer's phone area code was left blank by the operator — used to distinguish a missing entry from an incorrectly formatted one.
30 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1C PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the third digit segment of the customer's US phone area code. Tracks whether this portion of the area code passed, failed, or was left blank during the update screen validation process.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1C-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition flag confirming that the third digit segment of the customer's phone area code has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1C-NOT-OK – '0' Condition flag indicating that the third digit segment of the customer's phone area code failed validation — the bank operator must correct this portion before the update can proceed.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-1C-BLANK – 'B' Condition flag indicating that the third digit segment of the customer's phone area code was left blank — distinguishes a missing entry from an incorrectly formatted one so the operator receives the appropriate error message.
20 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2-FLGS
Group field 		– – Group of validation status flags covering all three digit segments of the customer's US phone exchange (central office code — the middle three digits of the phone number). All segments must pass for the phone number to be accepted.
88 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2-IS-INVALID – – Composite condition flag that signals the entire phone exchange segment (middle three digits of the customer's US phone number) is invalid — used to block the account update and prompt the operator to correct the phone number.
30 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2A-FLG PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the first digit of the customer's US phone exchange segment. Tracks whether this digit passed, failed, or was left blank during screen input validation.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2A-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition flag confirming that the first digit of the customer's phone exchange segment has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2A-NOT-OK – '0' Condition flag indicating that the first digit of the customer's phone exchange segment failed validation — the operator must correct this before the update can be saved.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2A-BLANK – 'B' Condition flag indicating that the first digit of the customer's phone exchange segment was left blank — distinguishes a missing mandatory entry from an incorrectly formatted one.
30 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2B PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the second digit of the customer's US phone exchange segment. Tracks whether this digit passed, failed, or was left blank during screen input validation.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2B-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition flag confirming that the second digit of the customer's phone exchange segment has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2B-NOT-OK – '0' Condition flag indicating that the second digit of the customer's phone exchange segment failed validation — the operator must correct this before the update can be saved.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2B-BLANK – 'B' Condition flag indicating that the second digit of the customer's phone exchange segment was left blank — distinguishes a missing mandatory entry from an incorrectly formatted one.
30 WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2C PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the third digit of the customer's US phone exchange segment. Tracks whether this digit passed, failed, or was left blank during screen input validation.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2C-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition flag confirming that the third digit of the customer's phone exchange segment has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2C-NOT-OK – '0' Condition flag indicating that the third digit of the customer's phone exchange segment failed validation — the operator must correct this before the update can be saved.
88 FLG-PHONE-NUM-2C-BLANK – 'B' Condition flag indicating that the third digit of the customer's phone exchange segment was left blank — distinguishes a missing mandatory entry from an incorrectly formatted one.
10 WS-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-FLGS PIC X(01) – Validation status flag for the customer's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) bank account identifier — used when the customer has a linked external bank account for payments or direct debit. Tracks whether the EFT account ID entered on screen is valid, invalid, or blank.
88 FLG-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-ISVALID – LOW-VALUES Condition flag confirming that the customer's EFT bank account identifier has passed validation and can be saved to the customer record.
88 FLG-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-NOT-OK – '0' Condition flag indicating that the customer's EFT bank account identifier failed validation — the operator must correct this value before the update can proceed.
88 FLG-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-BLANK – 'B' Condition flag indicating that the customer's EFT bank account identifier was left blank on the update screen — distinguishes a missing entry from an incorrectly formatted one for appropriate error messaging.
10 WS-EDIT-PRI-CARDHOLDER PIC X(1) – Validation status flag indicating whether the customer being updated is designated as the primary cardholder on the account. Must be explicitly Y (yes, primary) or N (no, supplementary) — any other value or blank is rejected to ensure clear account ownership is recorded.
88 FLG-PRI-CARDHOLDER-ISVALID – 'Y', 'N' Condition flag confirming that the primary cardholder designation has been set to a valid value (Y or N) — the account update can proceed with this field as entered.
88 FLG-PRI-CARDHOLDER-NOT-OK – '0' Condition flag indicating that the primary cardholder designation contains an invalid value — the operator must enter Y or N before the update can be saved.
88 FLG-PRI-CARDHOLDER-BLANK – 'B' Condition flag indicating that the primary cardholder designation was left blank — this mandatory field must be completed before the account update can proceed.
05 CICS-OUTPUT-EDIT-VARS
Group field 		– – Group of working variables used to format and validate data before it is displayed on the account update screen or written to the database — acts as a staging area for converting raw input into properly formatted account and customer field values.
10 CUST-ACCT-ID-X PIC X(11) – The customer's account identifier held as a text string — used when displaying the account number on screen or when the account ID needs to be treated as character data for formatting or comparison purposes.
10 CUST-ACCT-ID-N
REDEFINES CUST-ACCT-ID-X 		– – The customer's account identifier reinterpreted as a numeric value — allows arithmetic operations or numeric comparisons on the same account ID field without duplicating storage, used during validation and database lookup.
10 WS-EDIT-DATE-X PIC X(10) – A general-purpose date field in display format (YYYY-MM-DD) used as a working area when validating or formatting dates entered on the account update screen — such as account open date, card expiry date, or customer date of birth.
10 FILLER
Group field
REDEFINES WS-EDIT-DATE-X 		– – Redefines the general-purpose date field to expose its individual components (year, separator, month, separator, day) so each part can be independently extracted and validated during date checking on the account update screen.
20 WS-EDIT-DATE-X-YEAR PIC X(4) – The four-digit year portion of a date being validated on the account update screen — used to check that the year component of dates such as account open date, card expiry, or date of birth is within an acceptable range.
20 FILLER PIC X(1) – The separator character (typically a hyphen) between the year and month portions of a date displayed on screen — not used for business logic but required to correctly parse the formatted date string.
20 WS-EDIT-DATE-MONTH PIC X(2) – The two-digit month portion of a date being validated on the account update screen — used to verify that the month component of dates such as account open date, card expiry, or date of birth is a valid calendar month (01–12).
20 FILLER PIC X(1) – The separator character (typically a hyphen) between the month and day portions of a date displayed on screen — not used for business logic but required to correctly parse the formatted date string.
20 WS-EDIT-DATE-DAY PIC X(2) – The two-digit day portion of a date being validated on the account update screen — used to verify that the day component of dates such as account open date, card expiry, or date of birth is a valid calendar day for the given month and year.
10 WS-EDIT-DATE-X – – A second redefinition of the general-purpose date working area — allows the same date storage to be accessed in an alternative format or structure during different stages of date validation and formatting on the account update screen.
10 WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2 PIC X(15) – A working area that holds a monetary amount as a character string — used as an intermediate buffer when receiving currency values (such as credit limit, cash limit, or current balance) from the screen before converting them to numeric format for validation and storage.
10 WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2-F PIC +ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.99 – A formatted numeric field used to display monetary amounts (such as credit limit, cash advance limit, or current balance) on the account update screen in a human-readable format with sign, comma separators, and two decimal places — ensures bank staff see properly formatted currency values.
05 WS-XREF-RID
Group field 		– – Cross-reference record identifier group — holds the key fields (card number, customer ID, account ID) needed to look up and link the credit card record, customer record, and account record across the three related database files during the update process.
10 WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM PIC X(16) – The 16-digit credit card number used as the primary key to locate the card record in the credit card file — this is the card number printed on the customer's physical card and is the starting point for retrieving all related account and customer information.
10 WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID PIC 9(09) – The nine-digit customer identifier used as the key to retrieve the customer's demographic record from the customer master file — links the credit card to the specific customer who holds it.
10 WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X
REDEFINES WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID 		– – The customer identifier reinterpreted as a character string — allows the numeric customer ID to be used in character-based comparisons, screen display, or file key construction without duplicating storage.
10 WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) – The eleven-digit account identifier used as the key to retrieve the financial account record from the account master file — links the credit card to the specific credit account holding the balance, limits, and status information.
10 WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X
REDEFINES WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID 		– – The account identifier reinterpreted as a character string — allows the numeric account ID to be used in character-based comparisons, screen display, or file key construction without duplicating storage.
05 WS-FILE-READ-FLAGS
Group field 		– – Group of flags that record whether the account master record and customer master record were successfully retrieved from the database — both records must be found before the update screen can be populated or any changes saved.
10 WS-ACCOUNT-MASTER-READ-FLAG PIC X(1) – Tracks whether the financial account master record was successfully read from the database for the account being updated — if the account cannot be found, the update cannot proceed and the operator is notified.
88 FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER – '1' Condition flag confirming that the account master record was successfully retrieved from the database — the program can proceed to display and update the account's financial details such as credit limit, balance, and status.
10 WS-CUST-MASTER-READ-FLAG PIC X(1) – Tracks whether the customer demographic master record was successfully read from the database for the customer linked to the account being updated — if the customer record cannot be found, the update cannot proceed.
88 FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER – '1' Condition flag confirming that the customer master record was successfully retrieved from the database — the program can proceed to display and update the customer's personal details such as name, address, date of birth, and SSN.
05 WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE
Group field 		– – A structured error message displayed to the bank operator when a database file operation (read, write, or update) fails — identifies which operation was attempted, which file was involved, and the system error response code so the operator or support team can diagnose the problem.
10 FILLER PIC X(12) – Fixed label text at the start of the file error message (e.g. 'ERROR ON ') — provides a readable prefix so the operator immediately recognises the message as a file access error.
10 ERROR-OPNAME PIC X(8) – The name of the database operation that failed (e.g. 'READ', 'WRITE', 'REWRITE') — tells the operator and support team exactly what action was being performed on the account or customer record when the error occurred.
10 FILLER PIC X(4) – Fixed spacing or label text between the operation name and file name in the error message — improves readability of the error displayed to the bank operator.
10 ERROR-FILE PIC X(9) – The name of the database file that experienced the error (e.g. the account master file or customer master file) — identifies which data store was being accessed when the failure occurred, helping support staff locate and resolve the issue.
10 FILLER PIC X(15) – Fixed spacing or label text between the file name and the error response code in the error message — improves readability of the error displayed to the bank operator.
10 ERROR-RESP PIC X(10) – The CICS system response code returned when the database operation failed — provides the technical error code that support staff can use to diagnose the exact nature of the file access failure (e.g. record not found, file unavailable, duplicate key).
10 FILLER PIC X(7) – Fixed trailing spacing or label text at the end of the file error message — pads the message to its full display length and may contain additional context text for the operator.
10 ERROR-RESP2 PIC X(10) – Stores the secondary CICS error response code when a file operation (such as reading or writing an account or customer record) fails. Used by bank staff support and developers to diagnose the exact reason a database update could not be completed — for example, why a card account record could not be saved.
10 FILLER PIC X(5) – Reserved padding space within the error response area. Has no direct business meaning; it ensures proper memory alignment of the surrounding error-handling fields so that error codes are read and written correctly.
05 ALPHA-VARS-FOR-DATA-EDITING
Group field 		– – A group of temporary text-format holding areas used during input validation. When a bank operator types financial amounts on the update screen, these fields capture the raw text before the program checks whether the values are valid numbers. This prevents the program from crashing on non-numeric input and allows meaningful error messages to be shown to the operator.
15 ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X PIC X(15) – Temporary text representation of the new credit limit amount entered by the bank operator on the account update screen. Held as plain text so the program can validate it is a proper numeric amount before applying it to the customer's account as the maximum total credit they are allowed to carry.
15 ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-X PIC X(15) – Temporary text representation of the new cash advance credit limit entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being applied to the account as the maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to withdraw as a cash advance.
15 ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-X PIC X(15) – Temporary text representation of the current outstanding balance entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being recorded as the cardholder's current amount owed on the account.
15 ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-X PIC X(15) – Temporary text representation of the total credits posted in the current billing cycle, as entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being recorded — this represents payments and credits applied to the account during the current statement period.
15 ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-X PIC X(15) – Temporary text representation of the total debits posted in the current billing cycle, as entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being recorded — this represents purchases and charges made on the account during the current statement period.
05 ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD
Group field 		– – The complete financial account record being prepared for update. This structure holds all validated account-level data that will be written to the credit card account master file once the bank operator confirms the changes. It represents the core financial profile of a credit card account.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-ID PIC 9(11) – The unique 11-digit account identifier for the credit card account being updated. This is the primary key used to locate and update the correct account record in the account master file — it uniquely identifies one customer's credit card account within the bank's system.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01) – Indicates whether the credit card account is currently active or inactive. Must be set to 'Y' (account is open and usable) or 'N' (account is closed or suspended). Bank operators use this to activate or deactivate a customer's account as part of account management.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-BAL PIC S9(10)V99 – The current outstanding balance on the credit card account, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. This is the total amount the cardholder currently owes to the bank, and can be negative (representing a credit in the customer's favor).
15 ACCT-UPDATE-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC S9(10)V99 – The maximum total credit limit approved for this credit card account, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. This is the highest balance the cardholder is permitted to carry — purchases that would exceed this limit should be declined.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC S9(10)V99 – The maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to withdraw as cash advances on this account, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. This sub-limit is typically lower than the overall credit limit and governs ATM and cash advance transactions.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-OPEN-DATE PIC X(10) – The date on which the credit card account was originally opened, stored in a 10-character format (YYYY-MM-DD). This is a key piece of account history used for tenure tracking, regulatory reporting, and determining how long the customer has held the account.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10) – The expiration date of the credit card associated with this account, stored in a 10-character format (YYYY-MM-DD). After this date the physical card is no longer valid for transactions, and a new card must be issued to the cardholder.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-REISSUE-DATE PIC X(10) – The date on which the credit card was most recently reissued or renewed to the cardholder, stored in a 10-character format (YYYY-MM-DD). This tracks when a replacement card was sent, which is important for card lifecycle management and fraud investigation.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-CYC-CREDIT PIC S9(10)V99 – The total amount of credits (payments, refunds, adjustments) posted to the account during the current billing cycle, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. Used in statement generation and balance calculation for the current period.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-CYC-DEBIT PIC S9(10)V99 – The total amount of debits (purchases, fees, interest charges) posted to the account during the current billing cycle, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. Used in statement generation and balance calculation for the current period.
15 ACCT-UPDATE-GROUP-ID PIC X(10) – An identifier linking this credit card account to a specific product group, pricing tier, or customer segment within the bank. This may determine which fee schedules, interest rates, or reward programs apply to the account.
15 FILLER PIC X(188) – Reserved padding space within the account update record to align the total record length with the physical account master file layout. Has no direct business meaning but ensures the record written to the database matches the expected file structure exactly.
05 CUST-UPDATE-RECORD
Group field 		– – The complete customer demographic record being prepared for update. This structure holds all validated personal and contact information about the cardholder that will be written to the customer master file once the bank operator confirms the changes. It represents the identity and contact profile of the customer.
15 CUST-UPDATE-ID PIC 9(09) – The unique 9-digit customer identifier for the individual whose demographic information is being updated. This is the primary key used to locate and update the correct customer record in the customer master file — it uniquely identifies one person within the bank's customer database.
15 CUST-UPDATE-FIRST-NAME PIC X(25) – The customer's legal first (given) name, up to 25 characters. Must contain alphabetic characters only. Used for customer identification, correspondence, and regulatory compliance — ensuring the bank addresses and identifies the cardholder correctly.
15 CUST-UPDATE-MIDDLE-NAME PIC X(25) – The customer's legal middle name, up to 25 characters. Must contain alphabetic characters only. Used to fully identify the customer, particularly when first and last names alone are insufficient to distinguish between customers with similar names.
15 CUST-UPDATE-LAST-NAME PIC X(25) – The customer's legal last (family/surname) name, up to 25 characters. Must contain alphabetic characters only. A mandatory identification field used across all customer communications, statements, and regulatory reporting.
15 CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-1 PIC X(50) – The first line of the customer's mailing address (typically street number and street name), up to 50 characters. Used for sending account statements, card mailings, and other bank correspondence to the cardholder's physical location.
15 CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-2 PIC X(50) – The second line of the customer's mailing address (typically apartment, suite, or unit number), up to 50 characters. Supplements the primary address line to ensure accurate mail delivery to the cardholder.
15 CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-3 PIC X(50) – The third line of the customer's mailing address (typically city name), up to 50 characters. Part of the complete address used for delivering statements and correspondence to the cardholder.
15 CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-STATE-CD PIC X(02) – The two-character US state code for the customer's mailing address (e.g., 'CA' for California, 'NY' for New York). Used to complete the mailing address and may also be used for state-level regulatory reporting and tax purposes.
15 CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD PIC X(03) – The three-character country code for the customer's mailing address (e.g., 'USA'). Identifies the country of residence for the cardholder, which is relevant for international compliance, sanctions screening, and cross-border regulatory requirements.
15 CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-ZIP PIC X(10) – The postal ZIP code for the customer's mailing address, up to 10 characters (accommodating both 5-digit and ZIP+4 formats). Used to complete the mailing address and may be used for geographic segmentation and fraud detection.
15 CUST-UPDATE-PHONE-NUM-1 PIC X(15) – The customer's primary contact phone number in US format, up to 15 characters. Used by the bank to contact the cardholder for account alerts, fraud verification, collections, and customer service. Must conform to standard US phone number format validation.
15 CUST-UPDATE-PHONE-NUM-2 PIC X(15) – The customer's secondary or alternate contact phone number in US format, up to 15 characters. Provides a backup contact method for the bank to reach the cardholder when the primary number is unavailable.
15 CUST-UPDATE-SSN PIC 9(09) – The customer's 9-digit US Social Security Number stored as a numeric value. This is a critical government-issued identity identifier used for regulatory compliance (e.g., KYC — Know Your Customer), credit bureau reporting, and uniquely verifying the customer's legal identity.
15 CUST-UPDATE-GOVT-ISSUED-ID PIC X(20) – An alternative government-issued identification number for the customer (such as a passport number or driver's license number), up to 20 characters. Used as a supplementary identity verification document, particularly for customers who may not have a US Social Security Number.
15 CUST-UPDATE-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD PIC X(10) – The customer's date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format. Used for identity verification, age eligibility checks (e.g., confirming the cardholder is of legal age), regulatory compliance, and fraud prevention. Must be a valid past calendar date.
15 CUST-UPDATE-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID PIC X(10) – The identifier for the customer's linked Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) bank account, up to 10 characters. This links the credit card account to a checking or savings account used for automatic payments, direct debits, or balance transfers.
15 CUST-UPDATE-PRI-CARD-IND PIC X(01) – A single-character indicator showing whether this customer record is associated with the primary cardholder on the account. Distinguishes the main account holder from authorized secondary cardholders, which affects billing responsibility and account privileges.
15 CUST-UPDATE-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE PIC 9(03) – The customer's FICO credit score, a 3-digit number typically ranging from 300 to 850. This score reflects the customer's creditworthiness and is used by the bank to assess lending risk, determine credit limits, and set interest rates on the account.
15 FILLER PIC X(168) – Reserved padding space within the customer update record to align the total record length with the physical customer master file layout. Has no direct business meaning but ensures the record written to the database matches the expected file structure exactly.
05 WS-LONG-MSG PIC X(500) – A large 500-character message area used to hold extended diagnostic or informational text. Used internally to construct detailed error descriptions or processing messages that may be logged or displayed when a complex validation failure or system error occurs during the account update process.
05 WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) – A 40-character field that holds the current instructional or status message displayed to the bank operator on the account update screen. Its value drives what guidance or feedback the operator sees at any given point in the update workflow.
88 WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE – – Condition indicating that no informational message is currently set for the operator. The screen message area is blank, meaning the program has not yet determined what guidance to show the bank operator.
88 FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA – – Condition indicating that the account and customer records were successfully retrieved from the database and are now displayed on screen. The bank operator can see the current account data and is ready to make changes.
88 PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS – – Condition indicating that the screen is prompting the bank operator to enter the account or customer identifier needed to look up the record they wish to update. The operator has not yet provided search criteria.
88 PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES – – Condition indicating that the account data has been loaded and the screen is now prompting the bank operator to enter the changes they wish to make to the account or customer record.
88 PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION – – Condition indicating that the operator's changes have passed validation and the screen is now asking the operator to confirm that they want to save the changes to the account and customer records. This is the final check before the database is updated.
88 CONFIRM-UPDATE-SUCCESS – – Condition indicating that the account and customer records were successfully updated in the database. The screen displays a success confirmation to the bank operator, confirming the changes have been saved.
88 INFORM-FAILURE – – Condition indicating that the update process failed — either due to a validation error or a database write failure. The screen informs the bank operator that the changes could not be saved and further action is required.
05 WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) – A 75-character message field used to pass a status or instructional message back to the calling menu program when the operator exits the account update screen. This message may inform the operator or the next screen about the outcome of the update session.
88 WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF – SPACES Condition indicating that no return message has been set. The operator is not being sent back to the calling program with any specific message — the return message area is blank.
88 WS-EXIT-MESSAGE – – Condition indicating that the return message is a general exit notification, signalling to the calling program that the operator has chosen to leave the account update screen and return to the menu.
88 WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT – – Condition indicating that the return message is instructing the operator (or the calling program) that an account number must be provided before the update process can begin. No account has been identified yet.
88 WS-PROMPT-FOR-LASTNAME – – Condition indicating that the return message is instructing the operator that a customer last name must be provided as a search criterion. The program requires this information to locate the correct customer record.
88 WS-NAME-MUST-BE-ALPHA – – Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that a name field they entered contains invalid characters — names must contain alphabetic characters only. The operator must correct the entry before the update can proceed.
88 NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED – – Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that they submitted the screen without entering any search criteria (account number or customer identifier). The program cannot look up a record without at least one search key.
88 NO-CHANGES-DETECTED – – Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that the data they submitted is identical to what is already stored in the database — no fields were actually changed. The program will not perform an unnecessary database write in this case.
88 SEARCHED-ACCT-ZEROES – – Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that the account number they entered consists entirely of zeros, which is not a valid account number. The operator must enter a real account identifier.
88 SEARCHED-ACCT-NOT-NUMERIC – – Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that the account number they entered contains non-numeric characters. Account numbers must be entirely numeric, and the operator must correct their entry before the search can proceed.
88 DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF – – Error condition indicating that the account number entered by the bank operator could not be found in the card cross-reference file (CARDXREF), meaning no credit card is linked to this account. The update cannot proceed because the account-to-card relationship does not exist.
88 DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT – – Error condition indicating that the account number entered by the bank operator does not exist in the account master file (ACCTDAT). The update cannot proceed because there is no financial account record to update.
88 DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT – – Error condition indicating that the customer number associated with the account cannot be found in the customer master file (CUSTDAT). The update cannot proceed because there is no customer demographic record to update alongside the account record.
88 ACCT-STATUS-MUST-BE-YES-NO – – Validation error condition indicating that the account status field entered by the operator contains an invalid value. Per business rules, account status must be exactly 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive) — any other entry is rejected.
88 CRED-LIMIT-IS-BLANK – – Validation error condition indicating that the credit limit field was left empty by the operator. Credit limit is a mandatory field — a blank submission is flagged as a distinct error separate from an invalid format error, preventing the account update from proceeding.
88 CRED-LIMIT-IS-NOT-VALID – – Validation error condition indicating that the credit limit amount entered by the operator is not a valid signed numeric value. The credit limit must be a properly formatted monetary amount before the account record can be updated.
88 THIS-MONTH-NOT-VALID – – Validation error condition indicating that a month component of a date field (such as account open date, card expiry date, reissue date, or customer date of birth) entered by the operator is not a valid calendar month (i.e., not between 01 and 12).
88 THIS-YEAR-NOT-VALID – – Validation error condition indicating that a year component of a date field (such as account open date, card expiry date, reissue date, or customer date of birth) entered by the operator is not a valid calendar year, preventing the account or customer record from being updated.
88 DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF – – Duplicate error condition flag (second occurrence) indicating that the account number could not be located in the card cross-reference file during a subsequent lookup step, confirming that no valid card-to-account linkage exists and the update must be aborted.
88 DID-NOT-FIND-ACCTCARD-COMBO – – Error condition indicating that the specific combination of account number and card number entered by the operator does not exist as a matched pair in the system. Even if each exists individually, the account-card pairing must be valid before any update is permitted.
88 COULD-NOT-LOCK-ACCT-FOR-UPDATE – – Error condition indicating that the system was unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the account master record for update. This typically means another bank operator or process is currently modifying the same account, and the update must be deferred to prevent data corruption.
88 COULD-NOT-LOCK-CUST-FOR-UPDATE – – Error condition indicating that the system was unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the customer master record for update. Similar to the account lock failure, this prevents simultaneous conflicting updates to the customer's demographic information by multiple operators.
88 DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE – – Error condition indicating that the account or customer data in the database was modified by another process between the time the operator retrieved the record for display and the time they submitted their changes. This protects against overwriting a more recent update with stale data.
88 LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED – – Error condition indicating a critical failure scenario where the system successfully locked the account or customer record for exclusive update but the actual write operation to the database subsequently failed. This requires operator notification and likely system investigation to ensure data integrity.
88 XREF-READ-ERROR – – Error condition indicating that an unexpected system error occurred while reading the card cross-reference file (CARDXREF) during the account lookup process. This is a technical file I/O failure rather than a business data validation error, and prevents the update from proceeding.
88 CODING-TO-BE-DONE – – Placeholder condition flag marking a section of the program where business logic has not yet been fully implemented. This is a development indicator used by programmers to identify incomplete functionality that still needs to be coded before the program is production-ready.
01 WS-LITERALS
Group field 		– – Group record containing all fixed constant values used throughout the account update program — including program names, transaction IDs, map names, file names, and character sets used for validation. These literals define the system's navigation targets and reference data used during the update process.
05 LIT-THISPGM PIC X(8) – The CICS program name of this account update program itself (COACTUPC). Used for self-identification in error messages, communication area routing, and CICS service calls so the system knows which program is currently executing.
05 LIT-THISTRANID PIC X(4) – The CICS transaction identifier for the account update transaction. This 4-character code is used by CICS to route terminal input to this program and is referenced when the program needs to re-invoke itself after returning control to the operator.
05 LIT-THISMAPSET PIC X(8) – The BMS mapset name containing the account update screen definition (COACTUP). Used when sending or receiving the account update screen to/from the bank operator's terminal.
05 LIT-THISMAP PIC X(7) – The specific BMS map name within the mapset that defines the layout of the account update screen. Used in CICS SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP commands to display and capture the account update form on the operator's terminal.
05 LIT-CARDUPDATE-PGM PIC X(8) – The CICS program name of the card update program that handles credit card-level detail updates. Used when the account update process needs to transfer control to update card-specific information linked to the account being modified.
05 LIT-CARDUPDATE-TRANID PIC X(4) – The CICS transaction ID for the card update transaction. Used to initiate or navigate to the card update function when the operator needs to update card-level details (such as expiry or reissue dates) in addition to account information.
05 LIT-CARDUPDATE-MAPSET PIC X(8) – The BMS mapset name for the card update screen. Referenced when navigating to the card update function so the correct screen layout is displayed to the operator for card-level data entry.
05 LIT-CARDUPDATE-MAP PIC X(7) – The specific BMS map name for the card update screen within its mapset. Used to display the card update form to the operator when card-level details need to be modified.
05 LIT-CCLISTPGM PIC X(8) – The CICS program name of the credit card list program. Used when the operator needs to navigate back to the list of credit cards associated with an account, typically after completing or cancelling an update.
05 LIT-CCLISTTRANID PIC X(4) – The CICS transaction ID for the credit card list transaction. Used to transfer control back to the card listing screen so the operator can select a different card or account to work with.
05 LIT-CCLISTMAPSET PIC X(7) – The BMS mapset name for the credit card list screen. Referenced when navigating back to the card list display so the correct screen layout is used.
05 LIT-CCLISTMAP PIC X(7) – The specific BMS map name for the credit card list screen. Used to display the list of cards to the operator when returning from the account update function.
05 LIT-MENUPGM PIC X(8) – The CICS program name of the main CardDemo menu program. Used when the operator presses a function key to exit the account update screen and return to the main application menu.
05 LIT-MENUTRANID PIC X(4) – The CICS transaction ID for the main menu transaction. Used to transfer control back to the CardDemo main menu when the operator chooses to exit the account update function.
05 LIT-MENUMAPSET PIC X(7) – The BMS mapset name for the main menu screen. Referenced when navigating back to the main menu so the correct screen layout is displayed to the operator.
05 LIT-MENUMAP PIC X(7) – The specific BMS map name for the main menu screen. Used to display the CardDemo main menu to the operator after they exit the account update function.
05 LIT-CARDDTLPGM PIC X(8) – The CICS program name of the card detail inquiry program. Used when the operator needs to navigate to view detailed information about a specific credit card associated with the account being updated.
05 LIT-CARDDTLTRANID PIC X(4) – The CICS transaction ID for the card detail inquiry transaction. Used to transfer control to the card detail display when the operator wants to review card-specific information.
05 LIT-CARDDTLMAPSET PIC X(7) – The BMS mapset name for the card detail screen. Referenced when navigating to the card detail display so the correct screen layout is used to present card information to the operator.
05 LIT-CARDDTLMAP PIC X(7) – The specific BMS map name for the card detail screen. Used to display detailed credit card information to the operator when they navigate to the card detail inquiry function.
05 LIT-ACCTFILENAME PIC X(8) – The CICS file name (DDname) of the account master file (ACCTDAT). Used in all CICS file I/O commands (READ, REWRITE) when reading or updating the financial account record — credit limit, balance, and status data.
05 LIT-CUSTFILENAME PIC X(8) – The CICS file name (DDname) of the customer master file (CUSTDAT). Used in all CICS file I/O commands when reading or updating the customer demographic record — name, address, SSN, date of birth, and phone number.
05 LIT-CARDFILENAME PIC X(8) – The CICS file name (DDname) of the credit card master file. Used when reading or updating card-level records such as card expiry dates and reissue dates associated with the account being updated.
05 LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH PIC X(8) – The CICS file name for the alternate index path into the card file keyed by account number. Used to look up credit card records using the account number as the search key, rather than the card number, enabling account-to-card navigation.
05 LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH PIC X(8) – The CICS file name for the account-path alternate index into the card cross-reference file (CARDXREF). Used to verify that a valid account-to-card cross-reference record exists before attempting to update account or card data.
05 LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM-X
Group field 		– – Group field containing the complete set of valid alphanumeric characters (uppercase letters, lowercase letters, and digits 0-9) used as the source reference in character translation and validation operations for fields such as customer name and address.
10 LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM-X
Group field 		– – Group field containing the complete set of valid alphabetic characters (uppercase and lowercase letters) used as the source reference when validating that customer name fields contain only alphabetic characters, as required by business rules.
15 LIT-UPPER PIC X(26) – The 26 uppercase letters A through Z, used as a reference string when validating that customer name fields (first, middle, last) contain only alphabetic characters. Part of the character set used in INSPECT or translation operations to enforce the alphabetic-only business rule.
15 LIT-LOWER PIC X(26) – The 26 lowercase letters a through z, used alongside the uppercase set when validating that customer name fields contain only alphabetic characters. Ensures that names entered in mixed case are accepted as valid.
10 LIT-NUMBERS PIC X(10) – The 10 numeric digit characters 0 through 9, used as a reference string when validating numeric fields such as SSN segments, phone number segments, and zip codes to ensure they contain only digit characters.
01 LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM PIC X(52) SPACES A 52-character working field (26 uppercase + 26 lowercase letters) used as the 'FROM' argument in character translation operations when validating that customer name fields contain only alphabetic characters. Initialized to spaces and populated at runtime with the valid alpha character set.
01 LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM PIC X(62) SPACES A 62-character working field (26 uppercase + 26 lowercase letters + 10 digits) used as the 'FROM' argument in character translation operations when validating that address fields and other alphanumeric fields contain only valid alphanumeric characters.
01 LIT-ALL-NUM-FROM PIC X(10) SPACES A 10-character working field containing digit characters 0-9, used as the 'FROM' argument in character translation operations when validating purely numeric fields such as SSN segments, phone number parts, and zip codes.
77 LIT-ALPHA-SPACES-TO PIC X(52) SPACES A 52-character target field of spaces used as the 'TO' argument paired with LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM in character translation operations. When translating a name field, any valid alphabetic character maps to a space, leaving only invalid characters visible for detection.
77 LIT-ALPHANUM-SPACES-TO PIC X(62) SPACES A 62-character target field of spaces used as the 'TO' argument paired with LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM in character translation operations. Used to detect invalid characters in address and other alphanumeric fields by translating all valid characters to spaces.
77 LIT-NUM-SPACES-TO PIC X(10) SPACES A 10-character target field of spaces used as the 'TO' argument paired with LIT-ALL-NUM-FROM in character translation operations. Used to detect non-numeric characters in fields like SSN segments and phone number parts by translating all valid digits to spaces.
01 WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
Group field 		– – The communication area (COMMAREA) used by this account update program to maintain state between CICS interactions (pseudo-conversational processing). It preserves the current screen data and processing stage across multiple operator interactions with the account update screen.
05 ACCT-UPDATE-SCREEN-DATA
Group field 		– – Group record within the communication area that holds the current state of the account update screen interaction, tracking what stage of the update process the operator is in — whether account details have been fetched, changes are being entered, or changes are awaiting confirmation.
10 ACUP-CHANGE-ACTION PIC X(1) – A single-character state indicator that tracks the current stage of the account update workflow. It controls whether the program should fetch and display account details, accept operator changes, or handle validation errors — driving the pseudo-conversational flow of the update process.
88 ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED – – Condition indicating that the account and customer details have not yet been retrieved from the database for display. When true, the program must first look up and display the current account information before the operator can make any changes.
88 ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS – S Condition (value 'S') indicating that the program is in the 'display details' stage — the account and customer information has been fetched from the database and is being shown to the operator for review before they make any modifications.
88 ACUP-CHANGES-MADE – E, N Condition (values 'E' or 'N') indicating that the operator has submitted changes to the account or customer data. The program is now in the validation and update processing stage, regardless of whether the changes passed validation ('N') or failed ('E').
88 ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK – E Condition (value 'E') indicating that the operator's submitted changes failed validation. The screen is redisplayed with error messages highlighting the invalid fields so the operator can correct them before the account update can be written to the database.
88 ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED – N Condition indicating that the bank operator has reviewed the proposed account/customer changes on screen but has NOT yet confirmed them for saving. The update is pending final approval — the system is waiting for the operator to explicitly confirm before writing to the database.
88 ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE – C Condition indicating that the operator confirmed the account/customer changes AND the database update completed successfully. Both the account financial record and the customer demographic record have been saved without error.
88 ACUP-CHANGES-FAILED – L F Composite condition indicating that the confirmed account/customer update attempt failed for any reason — either because the record could not be locked for exclusive update (L) or because the actual write to the database failed (F). Used to trigger error handling and notify the operator that changes were NOT saved.
88 ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR – L Condition indicating that the operator approved the update but the system could not obtain an exclusive lock on the account or customer record — likely because another bank operator or process is simultaneously accessing the same record. The update was blocked to prevent data corruption.
88 ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED – F Condition indicating that the operator approved the update and the record was locked, but the actual write operation to the account or customer master file failed due to a system or I/O error. The operator must be informed that despite confirmation, the changes were not persisted.
05 ACUP-OLD-DETAILS
Group field 		– – Group record holding the original 'before-image' snapshot of both the account financial data and the customer demographic data as they existed in the database before the operator made any changes. Used to detect whether any field was actually modified and to support change comparison logic.
10 ACUP-OLD-ACCT-DATA
Group field 		– – Group record holding the original snapshot of all account-level financial fields (account ID, status, balances, limits, dates, group) as read from the account master file before the operator's edits. Used to compare against new values to detect actual changes.
15 ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID-X PIC X(11) – The original credit card account number (11 characters, alphanumeric format) as it was read from the account master file. Stored as text to allow display and comparison; used to confirm which account record is being updated.
15 ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID-X 		– – Numeric redefinition of the original account number, allowing the program to perform numeric operations or comparisons on the account identifier that was originally stored in text format.
15 ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01) – The original active/inactive status of the credit card account as it existed before the operator's update. Valid values are Y (account is active and usable) or N (account is inactive/blocked). Retained to detect if the operator changed the account status.
15 ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL PIC X(12) – The original current outstanding balance on the credit card account, stored as a 12-character text string as read from the database. Retained to detect whether the operator has changed the balance amount during the update session.
15 ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL 		– – Numeric redefinition of the original current balance, allowing arithmetic comparisons or calculations on the balance amount that was stored in text format in the database snapshot.
15 ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC X(12) – The original total credit limit approved for this credit card account, stored as text as read from the account master file. Used to detect whether the bank operator has changed the customer's borrowing ceiling during the update.
15 ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT 		– – Numeric redefinition of the original credit limit, enabling numeric comparison or validation of the credit limit value that was stored in text format in the database snapshot.
15 ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT PIC X(12) – The original cash advance credit limit for this account as read from the database — the maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to withdraw as cash. Retained to detect if the operator has modified this sub-limit during the update.
15 ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT 		– – Numeric redefinition of the original cash advance credit limit, allowing numeric operations on the cash limit value that was stored in text format.
15 ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DATE PIC X(08) – The original date on which the credit card account was opened, stored as an 8-character string (YYYYMMDD format) as read from the account master file. Used to detect if the operator has changed the account opening date.
15 ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DATE-PARTS
Group field
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DATE 		– – Redefinition of the original account open date that breaks it into its individual year, month, and day components, enabling separate validation or comparison of each date part.
20 ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR PIC X(4) – The 4-digit year component of the original account opening date (e.g., 2019). Used to individually validate or compare the year portion of the account open date.
20 ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON PIC X(2) – The 2-digit month component of the original account opening date (01–12). Used to individually validate or compare the month portion of the account open date.
20 ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY PIC X(2) – The 2-digit day component of the original account opening date (01–31). Used to individually validate or compare the day portion of the account open date.
15 ACUP-OLD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(08) – The original expiry date of the credit card as stored in the database (YYYYMMDD format) — the date after which the card is no longer valid for transactions. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the card expiration date.
15 ACUP-OLD-EXPIRAION-DATE-PARTS
Group field
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-EXPIRAION-DATE 		– – Redefinition of the original card expiry date that splits it into year, month, and day components for individual validation or comparison of each date element.
20 ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR PIC X(4) – The 4-digit year component of the original card expiry date (e.g., 2025). Used to individually validate or compare the year the card expires.
20 ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON PIC X(2) – The 2-digit month component of the original card expiry date (01–12). Used to individually validate or compare the month the card expires.
20 ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY PIC X(2) – The 2-digit day component of the original card expiry date (01–31). Used to individually validate or compare the day the card expires.
15 ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DATE PIC X(08) – The original date on which the credit card was last reissued or renewed (YYYYMMDD format) as read from the database. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the card renewal date during the update.
15 ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DATE-PARTS
Group field
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DATE 		– – Redefinition of the original card reissue date that breaks it into year, month, and day components for individual validation or comparison of each date element.
20 ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR PIC X(4) – The 4-digit year component of the original card reissue/renewal date. Used to individually validate or compare the year the card was last renewed.
20 ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON PIC X(2) – The 2-digit month component of the original card reissue/renewal date (01–12). Used to individually validate or compare the month the card was last renewed.
20 ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY PIC X(2) – The 2-digit day component of the original card reissue/renewal date (01–31). Used to individually validate or compare the day the card was last renewed.
15 ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT PIC X(12) – The original total credit amount posted to the account during the current billing cycle (e.g., payments and refunds), stored as text as read from the database. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this cycle-to-date credit figure.
15 ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT 		– – Numeric redefinition of the original current-cycle credit total, enabling arithmetic operations or numeric comparisons on the cycle credit amount stored in text format.
15 ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT PIC X(12) – The original total debit amount posted to the account during the current billing cycle (e.g., purchases and fees), stored as text as read from the database. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this cycle-to-date debit figure.
15 ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT 		– – Numeric redefinition of the original current-cycle debit total, enabling arithmetic operations or numeric comparisons on the cycle debit amount stored in text format.
15 ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID PIC X(10) – The original group or product classification code assigned to this credit card account as read from the database (e.g., a portfolio segment or pricing tier identifier). Retained to detect if the operator has changed the account's group assignment.
10 ACUP-OLD-CUST-DATA
Group field 		– – Group record holding the original snapshot of all customer demographic fields (name, address, phone, SSN, date of birth, etc.) as read from the customer master file before the operator's edits. Used to compare against new values to detect actual changes to customer information.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID-X PIC X(09) – The original customer identification number (9 characters, alphanumeric format) as read from the customer master file. Links the account record to the specific customer whose personal details are being updated.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID
REDEFINES ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID-X 		– – Numeric redefinition of the original customer ID, allowing numeric operations or comparisons on the customer identifier that was stored in text format.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-FIRST-NAME PIC X(25) – The customer's original first (given) name as stored in the customer master file before the update. Retained to detect if the bank operator has changed the customer's first name, which must contain alphabetic characters only.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME PIC X(25) – The customer's original middle name as stored in the customer master file before the update. Retained to detect if the bank operator has changed the customer's middle name, which must contain alphabetic characters only.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-LAST-NAME PIC X(25) – The customer's original last (family) name as stored in the customer master file before the update. Retained to detect if the bank operator has changed the customer's surname, which must contain alphabetic characters only.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1 PIC X(50) – The first line of the customer's original mailing/residential address (typically street number and street name) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has updated the customer's primary address line.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2 PIC X(50) – The second line of the customer's original address (e.g., apartment number, suite, or building name) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this supplementary address detail.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 PIC X(50) – The third line of the customer's original address (typically city name or additional locality information) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this address component.
15 ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD PIC X(02) – The 2-character US state code of the customer's original address (e.g., CA, NY, TX) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the customer's state of residence.
